title: Centre for Development of Telematics excels in Intellectual Property creation with expanding portfolio of Patents and Awardees
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Communications Centre for Development of Telematics excels in Intellectual Property creation with expanding portfolio of Patents and Awardees C-DOT hosts annual IP Awards ceremony 2026 to honour 64 Scientists to recognise innovation and excellence achieved by C-DOT Delhi Campus 47 Patents, 3 Copyrights, and 8 Research papers achieved by C-DOT Delhi Campus acknowledged during IPR day function at C-DOT Delhi प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                31 JUL 2026 7:43PM by PIB Delhi The Centre for Development of Telematics (C-DOT), the premier telecom R&D centre of the Department of Telecommunications (DoT), Ministry of Communications, Government of India, successfully organised the Annual IP Awards Ceremony 2026 to recognise and celebrate outstanding contributions from its Delhi campus in the field of Intellectual Property (IP). The ceremony honoured C-DOT researchers and innovators whose pioneering work continues to strengthen India's indigenous telecom technology ecosystem and advance the nation's vision of technology-led growth. A total of 47 patents, 3 copyrights, and 8 research papers were recognised, with awards conferred upon 64 individuals for their innovation and excellence at C-DOT Delhi. The event recognised the outstanding contributions of researchers, engineers, and domain experts whose pioneering work has significantly strengthened C-DOT's intellectual property portfolio. With a steadily expanding patent portfolio and a growing number of innovators being recognised for their excellence, C-DOT continues to reinforce its position as a premier telecom R&D institution driving indigenous technological innovation. These accomplishments underscore the organisation's sustained commitment to research excellence, intellectual property creation, and the development of globally competitive technologies that contribute to India's vision of technological self-reliance and digital transformation. Congratulating the awardees, Dr. Rajkumar Upadhyay, CEO, C-DOT, said, “Innovation is the cornerstone of C-DOT's mission to build indigenous, secure and future-ready telecom technologies for the nation. Every patent, publication and intellectual asset created by our researchers strengthens India's technological sovereignty and reinforces our commitment to the vision of Aatmanirbhar Bharat. These awards recognise not only exceptional technical excellence but also the spirit of curiosity, perseverance and innovation that drives C-DOT's research ecosystem. I congratulate all the awardees and encourage them to continue developing transformative technologies that contribute to India's emergence as a global telecom innovation leader." Over the years, C-DOT has built a robust intellectual property portfolio spanning next-generation communication technologies, cybersecurity, quantum communications, disaster management systems, AI-driven telecom solutions and digital public infrastructure. C-DOT remains committed to translating research excellence into impactful technologies that address national priorities while enhancing India's competitiveness in the global telecommunications landscape. Recently, C-DOT also organised the Annual IP Awards Ceremony 2026 at its Bengaluru campus, where 78 innovators were honoured for their exceptional contributions to Intellectual Property creation. The ceremony recognised 36 patents, 18 copyrights, 9 trademarks, and 3 research papers, reflecting the depth and diversity of innovation across the organisation. Together, the IP Awards ceremonies at the Delhi and Bengaluru campuses highlight C-DOT's continued commitment on innovation, intellectual property creation, and the development of indigenous technologies that contribute to India's growing leadership in the telecommunications sector. title: TRAI Hosts Workshop to Improve Quality of Audit in Digital Addressable Systems ( DAS ) Ecosystem
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Communications TRAI Hosts Workshop to Improve Quality of Audit in Digital Addressable Systems ( DAS ) Ecosystem प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                31 JUL 2026 6:07PM by PIB Delhi The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) today organised a workshop for the training of empanelled audit firms for Digital Addressable Systems (DAS) audit. Hosted at TRAI Headquarters in New Delhi, the workshop underscores a major step toward promoting regulatory compliance and fostering greater transparency across the television broadcasting distribution ecosystem. Attended by TRAI-empanelled auditors and representatives from the broadcasting industry i.e. broadcasters as well as Distribution Platform Operators, the day-long workshop served as a valuable platform for exchanging observations, insights, learnings, and experiences gained during audit processes. The workshop was attended by 81 participants in physical mode and 52 participants through online mode. To address the issues related to audit framework, amendments to the Interconnection Regulation and audit Manual have been issued this year which are effective from 1 st April 2026. The salient features of the amended regulation include: Clearly defined timelines for audits; wherein distributors have to conduct audit and submit audit report to broadcasters by 30 th September every year. Audit is to be done on financial year basis in place of earlier calendar year. Broadcasters can depute their representative during audit to ensure transparency and credibility of the audit process. If broadcasters find inadequacies/discrepancies in audit report, they can seek clarifications from the auditor through DPO. Auditors must address the same in a time-bound manner. If broadcaster is not satisfied with these clarifications, it can get the audit conducted at its own cost, after obtaining approval of the Authority. In case a broadcaster does not receive the audit report by 30 th September from the distributor, it can cause audit of such a distributor. To promote ease of doing business, the requirement of annual audit at DPOs cost has been made optional for distributors with fewer than 30000 subscribers. However, broadcasters can get such DPOs audited at broadcasters’ cost. Quote from TRAI Chairman “ TRAI’s primary objective is to foster a fair and equitable environment for all stakeholders. Its regulatory decisions reflect a commitment to balancing the interests of broadcasters, distributors, and other service providers, while placing consumer welfare at the heart of the decision-making process ,” said Shri Anil Kumar Lahoti, Chairman, TRAI. He added, “Audits conducted by TRAI-empanelled auditors are essential to ensure that the systems deployed by Distribution Platform Operators (DPOs) conform to the prescribed technical requirements. The annual audit process verifies the accuracy of both technical and commercial reports, including subscriber declarations and compliance with addressable system requirements relating to Conditional Access Systems (CAS), Subscriber Management Systems (SMS), fingerprinting, and other regulatory provisions. By ensuring transparency, accountability, and adherence to established standards, these audits play a vital role in strengthening and sustaining a trust-based broadcasting ecosystem.” The workshop was convened following industry requests made to the Authority for periodic training of auditors on audit processes and procedures, and for improving the quality of audit reports by aligning audit outcomes with technical and commercial requirements. Sessions featured expert presentations by BECIL, audit firms, and industry stakeholders. ***** NJ/AR (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2292617) आगंतुक पटल  : 96 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: हिन्दी Ministry of Communications TRAI Hosts Workshop to Improve Quality of Audit in Digital Addressable Systems ( DAS ) Ecosystem प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: National Digitization Drive Workshop Strengthens India’s Manuscript Preservation Framework; Union Minister of Culture Calls for Sustained National Effort in Digitization
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Culture National Digitization Drive Workshop Strengthens India’s Manuscript Preservation Framework; Union Minister of Culture Calls for Sustained National Effort in Digitization Ministry of Culture organizes the National Digitization Drive Workshop in New Delhi under the Gyan Bharatam Mission प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                31 JUL 2026 4:46PM by PIB Delhi India’s manuscript heritage spanning philosophy, Ayurveda, literature, mathematics, yoga, and diverse knowledge systems reflects the civilizational ethos of “jñānam paramam dhyeyam .” To advance this legacy, the Ministry of Culture convened the National Digitization Drive Workshop at The Ashok, New Delhi, under the Gyan Bharatam Mission, with participation from over 200 representatives of States/UTs, Centres, custodians, scholars, experts, and technology partners. Appreciating the coordinated national effort, the Union Minister of Culture Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat, said that, with the proactive support from all States, UTs, Ministry officials, Centres and custodians, over 1.2 crore manuscripts have been reported, marking a remarkable national milestone. The Union Minister added that the workshop is a coordinated national effort to safeguard centuries‑old knowledge, our saṅkalpa to respect the past, guide the present, and protect the future. Our Puravajas and Rishi‑munis created manuscripts across all disciplines, and it is our responsibility to categorize, codify, and publish them for future generations. The Union Minister called for sustaining the national momentum and emphasized the need to maintain the current pace of work. He also said that digitization demands precision, discipline, and collaboration and stressed that preserving India’s knowledge systems with accuracy and integrity is a national responsibility. Shri Vivek Aggarwal, Secretary Culture, stressed the need for a time‑bound, systematic, and coordinated work with all stakeholders to ensure uniformity, quality assurance, and seamless integration across the country. title: Air Marshal Sandeep Thareja appointed as DGAFMS w.e.f. August 31, 2026
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Defence Air Marshal Sandeep Thareja appointed as DGAFMS w.e.f. August 31, 2026 प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                31 JUL 2026 7:46PM by PIB Delhi Government has appointed Air Marshal Sandeep Thareja, SM, VSM & Bar, presently serving as the Director General Medical Services (Air), as the Director General Armed Forces Medical Services (DGAFMS) with effect from the afternoon of August 31, 2026. He will assume the appointment upon the retirement of the incumbent DGAFMS Surgeon Vice Admiral Arti Sarin, PVSM, AVSM, VSM. An alumnus of the Armed Forces Medical College (AFMC), Pune, Air Marshal Sandeep Thareja was commissioned in December 1986. He obtained his MD in Medicine in 1997 and DM in Gastroenterology from the All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS), New Delhi in 2005, where he was awarded the Best DM Student Award. An outstanding military professional, he secured an 'A' grading in all military courses and is an alumnus of the National Defence College. Over a distinguished career spanning nearly four decades, the officer has made significant contributions across the clinical, academic, operational and administrative domains of the AFMS. He has held several prestigious appointments including Senior Consultant (Medicine) at the Office of the DGAFMS, Commandant of Military Hospital Pathankot, Commandant of Command Hospital Lucknow, Director & Commandant of AFMC, Pune, in addition to Director General Medical Services (Air). As Director General Medical Services (Air), Air Marshal Thareja has steered several transformational initiatives to enhance operational medical preparedness. His efforts strengthened the AFMS' medical preparedness for India's Gaganyaan Human Spaceflight Mission and led the operationalisation of the BHISHM Cube, significantly enhancing rapid medical response capabilities for operational and humanitarian missions. An accomplished clinician, academician and teacher, Air Marshal Sandeep Thareja has guided numerous postgraduate and super-speciality students and has authored over 50 scientific publications in reputed national and international medical journals. In recognition of his distinguished service, he has been awarded the Sena Medal and the Vishisht Seva Medal twice (VSM & Bar). ***** VK/ Savvy (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2292700) आगंतुक पटल  : 144 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu Ministry of Defence Air Marshal Sandeep Thareja appointed as DGAFMS w.e.f. title: CHIEF OF THE ARMY STAFF LAUNCHES INDIGENOUS XTREME WEATHER GRADE DIESEL
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Defence CHIEF OF THE ARMY STAFF LAUNCHES INDIGENOUS XTREME WEATHER GRADE DIESEL प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                31 JUL 2026 2:18PM by PIB Delhi General Dhiraj Seth, Chief of the Army Staff (COAS), today launched the indigenously developed Xtreme Weather Grade (XWG) Diesel in New Delhi. Developed jointly by the Indian Army and Oil Marketing Companies, the specialised fuel will enhance the mobility, safety and operational availability of combat and logistics vehicles in extreme climatic conditions. The technology also has wider civilian use in high-altitude and severe winter regions and represents a significant step towards Atmanirbhar Bharat. Conventional diesel can thicken and clog fuel filters at very low temperatures, affecting the operation of vehicles in high-altitude and snow-bound areas. XWG Diesel overcomes this challenge and remains effective at temperatures as low as minus 42 degrees Celsius. Compliant with BS-VI standards and IS 1460:2025 specifications, it can be used in the Indian Army’s existing vehicle fleet without any engine modification or re-homologation. Speaking on the occasion, the COAS described XWG Diesel as a game-changing indigenous innovation that would enhance mobility, operational readiness and mission reliability across extreme climatic conditions. He highlighted that the fuel would eliminate practices, previously required to keep vehicles functional during severe winters, thereby improving the safety and morale of personnel. The COAS commended the Indian Army team and the Oil Marketing Companies,  for developing the solution within a year and expressed confidence that the collaboration would lead to further specialised fuels for diverse operational requirements. Beyond its military applications, the technology will also benefit the civilian users in high-altitude and extreme winter regions by improving the reliability and safety of vehicles and equipment operating under severe climatic conditions. ______________________________________________________________________ NA/PK (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2292330) आगंतुक पटल  : 707 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , Marathi , हिन्दी , Gujarati , Tamil , Telugu Ministry of Defence CHIEF OF THE ARMY STAFF LAUNCHES INDIGENOUS XTREME WEATHER GRADE DIESEL प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: IndiaAI and Ministry of AYUSH Sign MoU to Accelerate AI Innovation in Traditional Healthcare
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Electronics & IT IndiaAI and Ministry of AYUSH Sign MoU to Accelerate AI Innovation in Traditional Healthcare Partnership to enrich AIKosh with AYUSH health research artefacts and advance responsible AI for India's traditional medicine ecosystem प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                31 JUL 2026 3:45PM by PIB Delhi IndiaAI, Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), has signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the Ministry of AYUSH to accelerate the adoption of Artificial Intelligence (AI) across India's traditional medicine ecosystem. The collaboration marks a significant step towards strengthening AI research and innovation by integrating eligible AYUSH health research artefacts with AIKosh, India's sovereign AI repository. The MoU was signed by Shri Sudeep Srivastava, Chief Operating Officer, IndiaAI Mission & Joint Secretary, Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) and Dr. Kavita Jain, Joint Secretary & Chief Vigilance Officer, Ministry of AYUSH, in the presence of senior officials from both organisations. As part of the collaboration, the Ministry of AYUSH will onboard AIKosh and contribute eligible anonymised health research artefacts, including datasets, metadata, AI models, toolkits and relevant use cases. These resources will enable researchers, startups, academic institutions and innovators to develop AI solutions aligned with national priorities while adhering to applicable data-sharing policies and regulatory requirements. The collaboration will also enable eligible stakeholders from the AYUSH ecosystem to leverage India's AI computing infrastructure through the IndiaAI Compute ecosystem, supporting advanced AI research and the development of scalable healthcare solutions. Shri Sudeep Srivastava highlighted that "MoU between IndiaAI and Ministry of Ayush is an important step in enrichment of AIkosh with datasets of traditional healthcare. Further, this collaboration of modern technology with our ancient wisdom will enable and empower researchers and practitioner of our traditional medicinal sciences." Reiterating the transformative role of AI in strengthening research and innovation across the AYUSH ecosystem, Dr. Kavita Jain said, “The integration of Artificial Intelligence with Ayush will open new avenues for evidence-based research, knowledge management and innovation. Our collaboration with IndiaAI will help leverage advanced AI capabilities across areas such as research, medicinal plants, drug administration and capacity building, making the Ayush ecosystem more technology-driven and future-ready.” The MoU will remain valid for an initial period of two years, with provision for automatic renewal upon mutual agreement. The collaboration does not involve any financial commitment or liability for either party. The collaboration marks a significant step towards integrating India's rich heritage of traditional medicine with cutting-edge Artificial Intelligence capabilities. By bringing together AIKosh's data ecosystem, advanced AI infrastructure, and the Ministry of AYUSH's research ecosystem, the partnership aims to accelerate innovation, enable evidence-based research, and foster the development of responsible AI solutions that strengthen India's healthcare landscape. It reflects the shared commitment of both organisations to harness AI for public good while advancing a secure, inclusive, and future-ready digital ecosystem. **** Vinod Kumar / Kanishk Sharma (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2292413) आगंतुक पटल  : 247 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी Ministry of Electronics & IT IndiaAI and Ministry of AYUSH Sign MoU to Accelerate AI Innovation in Traditional Healthcare Partnership to enrich AIKosh with AYUSH health research artefacts and advance responsible AI for India's traditional medicine ecosystem प्रविष्टि तिथि:

ministry: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
title: CAQM issues Amendment to Direction No. 98 extending timeline for implementation of Revised PM emission Standards for Industries across Delhi-NCR
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change CAQM issues Amendment to Direction No. 98 extending timeline for implementation of Revised PM emission Standards for Industries across Delhi-NCR प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                31 JUL 2026 7:26PM by PIB Delhi The Commission for Air Quality Management in NCR and Adjoining Areas (CAQM) issued an Amendment to its Statutory Direction No. 98 regarding implementation of the revised Particulate Matter (PM) emission standards for industries operating across Delhi-NCR. The revised PM emission standard would now come into effect from 01.10.2026. The amendment was issued after consideration of the recommendations of the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) and representations received from industries and industrial associations in relation to the prevailing status of compliance with the revised emission norms. The Direction No. 98, notified on 20.02.2026, had prescribed a uniform and stringent PM emission standard of 50 mg/Nm³ for identified categories of industries across Delhi-NCR, based on technical recommendations of CPCB and studies undertaken by IIT Kanpur. The Commission reiterated that the revised PM emission standard continues to remain technically achievable and environmentally necessary for reducing industrial emissions and improving ambient air quality in the region. Subsequent to issuance of the Direction, CPCB, in coordination with the NCR State Pollution Control Boards (SPCBs) and the Delhi Pollution Control Committee (DPCC), undertook extensive efforts to facilitate compliance, including issuance of Directions to the concerned agencies, development of a dedicated online portal for monitoring installation and retrofitting of Air Pollution Control Devices (APCDs) and periodic review of the implementation status. During this process, industry associations highlighted certain practical challenges in meeting the prescribed timelines, including extended procurement and installation periods for APCDs, limited availability of agencies for adequacy assessment and capacity constraints of recognized laboratories for compliance verification. CPCB accordingly recommended extension of the compliance timelines as stipulated in Direction No. 98. After examining all relevant submissions, the CAQM concluded that a limited extension of the implementation timeline would facilitate effective and uniform compliance by industries without compromising the objective of reducing industrial emissions. Accordingly, through the Amendment to Direction No. 98, the Commission revised the implementation schedule and stipulated that the revised PM emission standard of 50 mg/Nm³ would now become applicable to all industries covered under Clause 21(i) of Direction No. 98 with effect from 01.10.2026. All other provisions, stipulations and conditions contained in Direction No. 98 dated 20th February 2026 would remain unchanged. The amendment is intended solely to provide additional time for industries to complete the necessary installation, retrofitting and assessment of APCDs, while ensuring full compliance with the stringent particulate matter emission standards within the revised timeline. ***** VM/SK (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2292690) आगंतुक पटल  : 72 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change CAQM issues Amendment to Direction No. 98 extending timeline for implementation of Revised PM emission Standards for Industries across Delhi-NCR प्रविष्टि तिथि:

ministry: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
title: NBA releases over ₹24 Lakh as Benefit Sharing to Farmers, Research Institutions and State Biodiversity Boards
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change NBA releases over ₹24 Lakh as Benefit Sharing to Farmers, Research Institutions and State Biodiversity Boards प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                31 JUL 2026 5:12PM by PIB Delhi The National Biodiversity Authority has released over ₹24 lakh as Access and Benefit Sharing (ABS) amount to benefit claimers, including buffalo farmers in Haryana, beneficiaries across 11 States, and three national research institutions. The amount has been released for conserving valuable biological resources that were later used by companies and research organisations for commercial utilisation. This demonstrates that farmers, breeders and institutes who conserve biological resources can receive fair and equitable benefit-sharing when their biological resources are used commercially. The benefit-sharing amount has been disbursed among the identified beneficiaries including a family-run Murrah Buffalo Farm, Haryana (Rs. 4.30 lakh); ICAR–National Bureau of Plant Genetic Resources (NBPGR), New Delhi (Rs. 4.61 lakh); ICRISAT, Patancheru, Hyderabad (Rs. 5.36 lakh); ICAR–National Bureau of Fish Genetic Resources (NBFGR), Lucknow (Rs. 0.14 lakh); and the State Biodiversity Boards of Maharashtra (Rs. 3.22 lakh), Gujarat (Rs. 1.92 lakh), Telangana (Rs. 1.52 lakh), Karnataka (Rs. 0.73 lakh), Rajasthan (Rs. 0.63 lakh), Andhra Pradesh (Rs. 0.54 lakh), Madhya Pradesh (Rs. 0.46 lakh), Haryana (Rs. 0.44 lakh), Punjab (Rs. 0.19 lakh), Odisha (Rs. 0.17 lakh) and Tamil Nadu (Rs. 0.13 lakh). The payment relates to access provided to Murrah buffalo breeding stock, one of India’s most commercial dairy buffalo breeds; hundreds of crop varieties, including rice, mustard, wild mung bean, chilli, tomato, cucumber, carrot, okra and other crops; 627 varieties of pearl millet; 55 maize varieties and fish cell cultures used in scientific research and cotton varieties. Under the National Biodiversity Authority’s ABS framework, benefit-sharing payments are disbursed in accordance with the approved regulations. The amounts allocated to research institutions will be utilized for biodiversity conservation and research activities. The ABS amount received from access to cotton genetic resources is distributed among the 11 cotton-growing States. In the case of individual conservers, such as farmers and breeders, the major share of the benefit-sharing amount is transferred through the concerned State Biodiversity Board for disbursement to the beneficiaries. With this release, the NBA has disbursed a total of around ₹153 crore as Access and Benefit Sharing payments, reinforcing India’s commitment to  strengthen conservation, maintain biological collections, support scientific research, improve taxonomic studies, undertake biodiversity surveys and build capacity for biodiversity conservation. This would ensure that those who conserve the country’s biological resources receive a fair share of the benefits arising from their use. ***** VM/SK (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2292523) आगंतुक पटल  : 185 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change NBA releases over ₹24 Lakh as Benefit Sharing to Farmers, Research Institutions and State Biodiversity Boards प्रविष्टि तिथि:

With this release, the NBA has disbursed a total of around ₹153 crore as Access and Benefit Sharing payments, reinforcing India’s commitment to  strengthen conservation, maintain biological collections, support scientific research, improve taxonomic studies, undertake biodiversity surveys and build capacity for biodiversity conservation. This would ensure that those who conserve the country’s biological resources receive a fair share of the benefits arising from their use. ***** VM/SK (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2292523)

title: Favara-UPI Cross-Border Payment Corridor Goes Live Between Maldives and India
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Finance Favara-UPI Cross-Border Payment Corridor Goes Live Between Maldives and India Individuals from Maldives Can Now Transfer Funds In Real Time to UPI-enabled Bank Accounts in India Through Their Mobile Banking Applications प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                31 JUL 2026 1:35PM by PIB Delhi The Maldives Monetary Authority (MMA) announced the successful go-live of the integration between the Maldives Instant Payment System, ‘Favara’, and India’s Unified Payments Interface (UPI) on 30 th July 2026. This marks a transformative milestone in cross-border digital financial connectivity and bilateral economic cooperation between the Maldives and India. Salient features of the development: Real-Time Transfers: The new service enables individuals in the Maldives to transfer funds using Favara to beneficiaries in India in real time. Transactions are initiated in Maldivian Rufiyaa (MVR) and credited to recipients in Indian Rupees (INR) through UPI. Initial Phase Participation: The service has commenced with the participation of two local banks: Bank of Maldives Plc and Maldives Islamic Bank Plc. Customers of these banks can initiate person-to-person (P2P) transfers directly to UPI-enabled bank accounts in India using their mobile banking applications and the Favara payment rail. Permitted Categories: Permitted remittance categories include family-maintenance-related remittances under both Foreign Inward and Foreign Outward Remittance, as well as gift-related remittances permitted under Foreign Outward Remittance. Collaborative Achievement: The implementation reflects close collaboration between the MMA, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), NPCI International Payments Limited (NIPL), participating financial institutions, and other stakeholders in both countries Background and Future Outlook The agreement for the Favara-UPI integration was executed between NIPL and MMA in July 2025. Following an accelerated 10-day timeline for testing, certification, onboarding, and live validation, the corridor achieved full operational readiness. Subsequent phases of the collaboration will introduce additional cross-border payment use cases, including QR-based merchant payments and other innovative digital payment services, further strengthening economic and financial ties between the Maldives and India. UPI is accepted in the following Nine countries: Cambodia, Singapore, United Arab Emirates, France, Mauritius, Nepal, Bhutan, Qatar and Sri Lanka - enabling Indian travellers to make seamless payments abroad through UPI. ***** SR/AD (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2292288) आगंतुक पटल  : 477 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी , Bengali , Gujarati , Tamil , Telugu , Malayalam Ministry of Finance Favara-UPI Cross-Border Payment Corridor Goes Live Between Maldives and India Individuals from Maldives Can Now Transfer Funds In Real Time to UPI-enabled Bank Accounts in India Through Their Mobile Banking Applications प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: Steps Taken for Strengthening Allied Healthcare Workforce
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Health and Family Welfare Steps Taken for Strengthening Allied Healthcare Workforce National Commission for Allied and Healthcare Profession has finalized 18 competency-based curriculums Online enrolment portals for professionals and institutions were made live in October 2024 to facilitate central and state-level workforce mapping 29 States/UTs have constituted State Allied and Healthcare Councils for implementation and execution of provisions under NCAHP Act, 2021 Union Government announced additional 100,000 AHPs over next five years in Budget 2026 Rs. 1,000 Crore has been allocated this year for Allied Health Care Professionals प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                31 JUL 2026 2:36PM by PIB Delhi The assessment and management of health workforce requirements is an ongoing and dynamic process carried out in coordination with State Governments and Union Territories based on evolving public health needs. To establish a robust statutory mechanism for regulating allied and healthcare professions across 57 recognized categories, the Government enacted the National Commission for Allied and Healthcare Professions (NCAHP) Act, 2021, and constituted the National Commission for Allied and Healthcare Profession (NCAHP) under the provisions of the Act. NCAHP has finalized 18 competency-based curriculum and online enrolment portals for professionals and institutions were made live in October 2024 to facilitate central and state-level workforce mapping. Furthermore, 29 States/UTs have constituted State Allied and Healthcare Councils for implementation and execution of the provisions under the Act. To address the evolving demands for AHPs in healthcare ecosystem, the Central Government in Budget Announcement 2026, announced addition of 100,000 AHPs over next five years. Further, an amount of Rs.1000 Crore has been allocated in this year for the Scheme for Allied Health Care Professionals. The Union Minister of State for Health and Family Welfare, Smt. Anupriya Patel stated this in a written reply in the Lok Sabha today. **** SR HFW/PQ-Steps taken for Strengthening Allied Healthcare Workforce/31 July 2026/3 (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2292345) आगंतुक पटल  : 176 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी Ministry of Health and Family Welfare Steps Taken for Strengthening Allied Healthcare Workforce National Commission for Allied and Healthcare Profession has finalized 18 competency-based curriculums Online enrolment portals for professionals and institutions were made live in October 2024 to facilitate central and state-level workforce mapping 29 States/UTs have constituted State Allied and Healthcare Councils for implementation and execution of provisions under NCAHP Act, 2021 Union Government announced additional 100,000 AHPs over next five years in Budget 2026 Rs. 1,000 Crore has been allocated this year for Allied Health Care Professionals प्रविष्टि तिथि:

ministry: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
title: Update on Pradhan Mantri Surakshit Matritva Abhiyan
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Health and Family Welfare Update on Pradhan Mantri Surakshit Matritva Abhiyan Since its inception in 2016, more than 7.91 crore pregnant women received antenatal care services and more than 1.24 crore high-risk pregnancies have been identified India's Maternal Mortality Ratio has declined by 43 points from 130 per one lakh live births in SRS (2014–16) to 87 per one lakh live births in SRS (2022–24) First trimester antenatal registration of India increased from 58.6% in NFHS-4 (2015-16) to 76.2% in NFHS-6 (2023-24) Mothers receiving four or more antenatal care visits in India increased significantly from 51.2% in NFHS-4 to 65.2% in NFHS-6 Institutional deliveries in India increased from 78.9% in NFHS-4 to 90.6% in NFHS-6 प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                31 JUL 2026 2:35PM by PIB Delhi The salient features of Pradhan Mantri Surakshit Matritva Abhiyan are as follows: Pradhan Mantri Surakshit Matritva Abhiyan (PMSMA) provides a fixed day, free of cost, assured and quality Antenatal Care on the 9 th day of every month. Under PMSMA, all pregnant women are provided services including drugs, laboratory investigations, ultrasound, and antenatal check-up by the OBGY specialist/ Medical Officer at designated Public Health facilities including DH, SDH, CHC-FRUs, non-CHC-FRUs, and PHCs. Obstetricians/ physicians from private sector and retired OBGY specialists are encouraged to provide voluntary services at designated public health facilities on the 9th of every month. Group Counselling is also provided to all pregnant women for diet, sleep, regular ANC check-up, institutional delivery, and breastfeeding including awareness about supplementary nutrition. Information Education & Communication (IEC), Inter-personal Communication (IPC) and Behaviour Change Communication (BCC) activities are undertaken. The progress made under Pradhan Mantri Surakshit Matritva Abhiyan (PMSMA) since its launch and improvement in maternal health indicators are as follows: Since its inception (2016), more than 7.91 crore pregnant women received antenatal care services and more than 1.24 crore high-risk pregnancies have been identified. As per the Sample Registration System (SRS), India's Maternal Mortality Ratio (MMR) has declined by 43 points from 130 per one lakh live births in SRS (2014–16) to 87 per one lakh live births in SRS (2022–24). First trimester antenatal registration of India increased from 58.6% in NFHS-4 (2015-16) to 76.2% in NFHS-6 (2023-24). Mothers receiving four or more antenatal care visits in India increased significantly from 51.2% in NFHS-4 (2015-16) to 65.2% in NFHS-6 (2023-24). Institutional deliveries in India increased from 78.9% in NFHS-4 (2015-16) to 90.6% in NFHS-6 (2023-24). Government of India has adopted several approaches under the Abhiyan for early identification, referral and management of high-risk pregnancies, including the expansion of condition screened and the individual tracking of such pregnancies under the extended e-PMSMA strategy until a healthy outcome of mother and child. The key steps are as follows: PMSMA is based on a fixed day strategy, and it provides free of cost assured and quality antenatal check up by a Specialist/Medical Officer on the 9th day of every month. Early identification and clinical management of High-Risk Pregnancies (HRPs) through comprehensive antenatal check-ups. Name-based tracking of every identified High-Risk Pregnancy until 45 days after delivery, ensuring healthy outcome for both the mother and the new-born across all States/UTs under extended e-PMSMA. Provision of three additional antenatal check-ups for all HRPs, screened by Medical Officers /Obstetricians to monitor maternal and foetal well-being. Automated SMS alerts to beneficiaries and ASHAs at the time of HRP registration, reminders for scheduled visits, and follow-up appointments. Linkage of HRPs to the nearest First Referral Units (FRUs) to ensure safe delivery and timely management of complications. Provision of incentives for High-Risk Pregnant Women towards free transportation to attend follow-up ANC visits. The following steps have been taken by the Government to encourage the private sector specialists and volunteer doctors to extend their services voluntarily to pregnant women under the Abhiyan: Provision of ‘I PledgeFor9’ Achievers Awards for acknowledging voluntary contributions by private doctors for PMSMA. Centralised PMSMA Portal has been created for registering private practitioners. Participation of professional organisations viz. FOGSI (Federation of Obstetric and Gynaecological Societies of India), IMA (Indian Medical Association). The Government has taken several measures to further strengthen PMSMA, particularly in rural and remote areas of the country. These include: Provision of additional PMSMA sessions beyond the designated 9th day of every month under the Extended Pradhan Mantri Surakshit Matritva Abhiyan (e-PMSMA) for timely follow-up and continuity of antenatal care for high-risk pregnant women. Strengthening of individual name-based line listing, tracking, and monitoring of identified high-risk pregnancies through the centralized PMSMA Portal. Capacity building of healthcare providers at all levels for early identification, risk stratification, timely referral, and appropriate management of high-risk pregnancies. Early identification of high-risk pregnancies and referral linkages for timely management of obstetric complications and prevent adverse maternal and neonatal outcomes. Provision of case-based incentives to ASHAs for mobilizing and follow-up of high-risk pregnant women, along with transport incentives for beneficiaries to facilitate attendance at scheduled antenatal care (ANC) visits. Regular monitoring and review of programme implementation at National and State levels to improve service delivery and coverage. Promoting awareness through regular Information, Education and Communication (IEC) and Behaviour Change Communication (BCC) activities. The Union Minister of State for Health and Family Welfare, Smt. Anupriya Patel stated this in a written reply in the Lok Sabha today. ***** SR HFW/PQ-Update on PMSMA/31 July 2026/1 (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2292344) आगंतुक पटल  : 216 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी Ministry of Health and Family Welfare Update on Pradhan Mantri Surakshit Matritva Abhiyan Since its inception in 2016, more than 7.91 crore pregnant women received antenatal care services and more than 1.24 crore high-risk pregnancies have been identified India's Maternal Mortality Ratio has declined by 43 points from 130 per one lakh live births in SRS (2014–16) to 87 per one lakh live births in SRS (2022–24) First trimester antenatal registration of India increased from 58.6% in NFHS-4 (2015-16) to 76.2% in NFHS-6 (2023-24) Mothers receiving four or more antenatal care visits in India increased significantly from 51.2% in NFHS-4 to 65.2% in NFHS-6 Institutional deliveries in India increased from 78.9% in NFHS-4 to 90.6% in NFHS-6 प्रविष्टि तिथि:

ministry: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
title: Steps taken to Strengthen Public Healthcare in Rural Areas
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Health and Family Welfare Steps taken to Strengthen Public Healthcare in Rural Areas Free Drugs Service Initiative rolled out under NHM which includes financial support to States/UTs for 113 drugs at Sub Health Centre level, 179 at Primary Health Centre level, 301 at Community Health Centre level, 318 at Sub District Hospital level and 381 drugs at district Hospitals ‘Free Diagnostics Service Initiative’ programme under NHM aim to provide accessible and affordable pathological and radiological diagnostics services closer to the community reducing Out-of-Pocket Expenditure Diagnostics services are provided free of cost at all levels of public health facilities: 14 tests at Sub Centers, 63 at Primary Health Centers, 97 at Community Health Centres, 111 tests at Sub District Hospitals and 134 tests at District Hospitals Various incentives and honorarium are provided under NHM to ensure quality and timely healthcare services in all Government hospitals प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                31 JUL 2026 2:33PM by PIB Delhi Health is a State subject. The primary responsibility of strengthening public healthcare system lies with the respective State/UT Governments. The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare provides technical and financial support to the States/UTs to strengthen the public healthcare system in rural areas based on the proposals received in the form of Programme Implementation Plans (PIPs) under National Health Mission. Government of India provides approval for the proposal in the form of Record of Proceedings (RoPs) as per norms & available resources. States/ UTs to ensure availability of HR by creating adequate number of regular posts as per the Indian Public Health Standards (IPHS) in the long run and using NHM posts in the short to medium term to fill critical gaps. The NHM supplements the regular human resources by filling up the gaps in human resources in secondary and primary care facilities (District Hospital and below) as per IPHS. The details of doctors, specialists, physicians, nurses and paramedical staff in Government hospitals and health centres across the country and their vacancies State/UT-wise can be accessed at the following link of HDI 2023-24: https://www.mohfw-dohfw.gov.in/static/uploads/2026/05/57202cf30629539e4d0fb0a2f700ac62.pdf To ensure availability of essential drugs and reduce the Out-of-Pocket Expenditure (OOPE) of the patients visiting the public health facilities, Government has rolled out the Free Drugs Service Initiative (FDSI) under National Health Mission. This includes financial support to States/UTs for 113 drugs at Sub Health Centre level, 179 at Primary Health Centre level, 301 at Community Health Centre level, 318 at Sub District Hospital level and 381 drugs at district Hospitals. This Ministry supports ‘Free Diagnostics Service Initiative’ programme under NHM with the aim to provide accessible and affordable pathological and radiological diagnostics services closer to the community, which in turn reduces the Out-of-Pocket Expenditure (OOPE). Diagnostics services are provided free of cost at all levels of public health facilities (14 tests at Sub Centers, 63 at Primary Health Centers, 97 at Community Health Centres, 111 test at Sub District Hospitals and 134 tests at District Hospitals). Under NHM, following types of incentives and honorarium are provided to ensure quality and timely healthcare services in all Government hospitals: Hard area allowances to specialist doctors for serving in rural and remote areas and for their residential quarters so that they find it attractive to serve in public health facilities in such areas. Honorarium to Gynecologists/ Emergency Obstetric Care (EmOC) trained, Pediatricians & Anesthetist/ Life Saving Anaesthesia Skills (LSAS) trained doctors is also provided to increase availability of specialists for conducting Cesarean Sections in rural & remote area. Incentives like special incentives for doctors, incentive for Auxiliary Nurse and Midwife (ANM) for ensuring timely Antenatal Checkup (ANC) checkup and recording, incentives for conducting Adolescent Reproductive and Sexual Health activities. States are also allowed to offer negotiable salary to attract specialist including flexibility in strategies such as “You Quote We Pay”. Non-Monetary incentives such as preferential admission in post graduate courses for staff serving in difficult areas and improving accommodation arrangement in rural areas have also been introduced under NHM. Multi-skilling of doctors is supported under NHM to overcome the shortage of specialists. Skill upgradation of existing HR is another major strategy under NRHM for achieving improvement in health outcomes. The Union Minister of State for Health and Family Welfare, Shri Prataprao Jadhav stated this in a written reply in the Lok Sabha today. **** SR HFW/PQ-Steps taken to Strengthen Public Healthcare in Rural Areas/31 July 2026/2 (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2292343) आगंतुक पटल  : 169 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी Ministry of Health and Family Welfare Steps taken to Strengthen Public Healthcare in Rural Areas Free Drugs Service Initiative rolled out under NHM which includes financial support to States/UTs for 113 drugs at Sub Health Centre level, 179 at Primary Health Centre level, 301 at Community Health Centre level, 318 at Sub District Hospital level and 381 drugs at district Hospitals ‘Free Diagnostics Service Initiative’ programme under NHM aim to provide accessible and affordable pathological and radiological diagnostics services closer to the community reducing Out-of-Pocket Expenditure Diagnostics services are provided free of cost at all levels of public health facilities: 14 tests at Sub Centers, 63 at Primary Health Centers, 97 at Community Health Centres, 111 tests at Sub District Hospitals and 134 tests at District Hospitals Various incentives and honorarium are provided under NHM to ensure quality and timely healthcare services in all Government hospitals प्रविष्टि तिथि:

ministry: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
title: Measures taken to Strengthen Food Testing System in the country

Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Health and Family Welfare Measures taken to Strengthen Food Testing System in the country FSSAI has notified 259 National Accreditation Board for Testing and Calibration Laboratories for analysis of food samples and 24 Referral Food Laboratories for the analysis of appeal samples Under the SoFTeL scheme, 47 State Food Testing Laboratories have been structurally upgraded with advanced analytical equipment and 34 specialized microbiology laboratories have been established to detect chemical, heavy metal and biological contaminants “Food Safety on Wheels” provides the widest outreach for food testing, training and awareness programme, especially in villages, towns and remote areas; Currently, 305 FSWs are deployed across 35 States/UTs “Magic Box” is a compact and user-friendly kit containing simple, rapid test methods to detect common food adulterants in seven different food commodities Detect Adulteration with Rapid Test book covers 44 tests that can be performed easily at household level with the help of water and simple solutions like tincture of iodine for various food products Rapid Analytical Food Testing Kits are advanced, easy to use, portable and handheld devices and don't require any sophisticated equipment or conventional reagents to conduct tests at the field level; 88 RAFT kits have been approved so far प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                31 JUL 2026 2:32PM by PIB Delhi Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) is mandated to lay down science-based standards for articles of food and to regulate their manufacture, storage, distribution, sale and import to ensure availability of safe and wholesome food for human consumption. The implementation and enforcement of the Food Safety and Standards (FSS) Act, 2006 is a shared responsibility between the Central and State Governments. For the safety of the food and food products through testing, FSSAI has notified 259 National Accreditation Board for Testing and Calibration Laboratories (NABL) for analysis of food samples and 24 Referral Food Laboratories for the analysis of appeal samples. The SoFTeL scheme i.e. Strengthening of Food Testing System in the Country including provision of Mobile Food Testing Laboratory (MFTL) is an initiative implemented by the FSSAI to upgrade state food laboratories, set up microbiology facilities and deploys mobile food testing vans. Under this scheme, 47 State Food Testing Laboratories have been structurally upgraded with advanced analytical equipment and 34 specialized microbiology laboratories have been established to detect chemical, heavy metal and biological contaminants. MFTL or “Food Safety on Wheels” (FSW) provides the widest outreach for food testing, training and awareness programme, especially in the villages, towns and remote areas. Currently, 305 FSWs are deployed across 35 States/UTs. The “Magic Box” is a compact and user-friendly kit containing simple, rapid test methods to detect common food adulterants in seven different food commodities. It aims to identify adulteration in everyday food items such as milk, spices, oils, and grains. Detect Adulteration with Rapid Test (DART) book covers 44 tests that can be performed easily at household level with the help of water and simple solutions like tincture of iodine for food products like Milk & Milk Products, Oils & Fats, Sugar & Confectionary, Food Grains & its products, Spices & Condiments etc. These tests also include sensory evaluation tests for establishing authentication of food products. DART book depicts the differences between pure and adulterated food product through pictorial representation. Also, Rapid Analytical Food Testing (RAPID) Kits are advanced, easy to use, portable and handheld devices and don't require any sophisticated equipment or conventional reagents to conduct the tests. So far, 88 RAFT kits have been approved. These kits help to reduce the screening time of the food products at the field level and thereby accelerate surveillance as well as monitoring activities. The Union Minister of State for Health and Family Welfare, Shri Prataprao Jadhav stated this in a written reply in the Lok Sabha today. ******* SR HFW/PQ-Measures taken to Strengthen Food Testing System in the country/31 July 2026/4 (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2292341) आगंतुक पटल  : 138 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी , Tamil Ministry of Health and Family Welfare Measures taken to Strengthen Food Testing System in the country FSSAI has notified 259 National Accreditation Board for Testing and Calibration Laboratories for analysis of food samples and 24 Referral Food Laboratories for the analysis of appeal samples Under the SoFTeL scheme, 47 State Food Testing Laboratories have been structurally upgraded with advanced analytical equipment and 34 specialized microbiology laboratories have been established to detect chemical, heavy metal and biological contaminants “Food Safety on Wheels” provides the widest outreach for food testing, training and awareness programme, especially in villages, towns and remote areas; Currently, 305 FSWs are deployed across 35 States/UTs “Magic Box” is a compact and user-friendly kit containing simple, rapid test methods to detect common food adulterants in seven different food commodities Detect Adulteration with Rapid Test book covers 44 tests that can be performed easily at household level with the help of water and simple solutions like tincture of iodine for various food products Rapid Analytical Food Testing Kits are advanced, easy to use, portable and handheld devices and don't require any sophisticated equipment or conventional reagents to conduct tests at the field level; 88 RAFT kits have been approved so far प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: Union Minister Shri Manohar Lal Chairs Parliamentary Consultative Committee Meeting on Urban Planning
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs Union Minister Shri Manohar Lal Chairs Parliamentary Consultative Committee Meeting on Urban Planning प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                31 JUL 2026 1:45PM by PIB Delhi Union Minister of Housing & Urban Affairs and Power, Shri Manohar Lal, chaired the Parliamentary Consultative Committee Meeting of the Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs (MoHUA) yesterday on the theme of Urban Planning. The meeting was attended by Minister of State for Housing & Urban Affairs, Shri Tokhan Sahu, Members of Parliament from both the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha, Secretary, Department of Capital Development (DCD), Ms. D. Thara, Secretary, Department of Urban Development (DUD), Shri Satendra Singh, senior officials of the Ministry, and other concerned officers. Secretary, Department of Capital Development, Ms. D. Thara, made a detailed presentation on the Ministry’s urban planning initiatives and the roadmap for sustainable urban development. During the meeting, the Union Minister informed the Members that the Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs will now function through two separate departments—the Department of Capital Development (DCD) (Rajdhani Vikas Vibhag) and the Department of Urban Development (DUD) (Shahari Vikas Vibhag). He stated that the restructuring has been undertaken to strengthen institutional capacity, improve administrative efficiency and enhance urban governance, enabling greater focus on the diverse and evolving needs of urban India. Addressing the Members, Shri Manohar Lal highlighted that the Ministry’s initiatives in urban planning are guided by the objective of creating liveable, resilient and citizen-centric cities. He emphasised that effective urban planning, robust urban governance, water security and continuous capacity building are essential for meeting the aspirations of India’s rapidly urbanising population and ensuring balanced urban growth. The Union Minister further underlined that the Ministry is adopting a holistic approach towards urban development by integrating planning, infrastructure, governance and service delivery. He noted that these efforts are aimed at improving the quality of life of citizens while building cities that are environmentally sustainable, economically vibrant and technologically enabled. Inviting suggestions from the Members of Parliament, Shri Manohar Lal reiterated the importance of collaborative policymaking and constructive dialogue in shaping the future of India’s cities. He assured the Members that their valuable suggestions would be duly considered in strengthening the Ministry’s policies and programmes. Reaffirming the PM Shri Narendra Modi’s vision of Viksit Bharat by 2047, Shri Tokhan Sahu stated that the Ministry is working closely to promote planned, sustainable and future-ready urban development across the country. Members of the Parliamentary Consultative Committee shared their views and suggestions on various aspects of urban planning and governance. The Union Minister welcomed their inputs and assured that appropriate follow-up action would be taken to further strengthen the Ministry’s initiatives in the urban sector. *** SK (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2292300) आगंतुक पटल  : 198 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: हिन्दी , Punjabi , Gujarati Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs Union Minister Shri Manohar Lal Chairs Parliamentary Consultative Committee Meeting on Urban Planning प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: Jan Bhagidari Powers Groundwater Revival in Vizianagaram under Jal Sanchay Jan Bhagidari: Catch the Rain
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Jal Shakti Jan Bhagidari Powers Groundwater Revival in Vizianagaram under Jal Sanchay Jan Bhagidari: Catch the Rain प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                31 JUL 2026 5:57PM by PIB Delhi Inspired by the Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi's appeal in the 135th edition of Mann Ki Baat to sustain the momentum of "Catch the Rain", communities across the country have intensified efforts under the Jal Sanchay Jan Bhagidari: Catch the Rain (JSJB:CTR) campaign. Vizianagaram district of Andhra Pradesh has emerged as a compelling example of how Jan Bhagidari, coupled with scientific water management and convergence of government programmes, can significantly enhance groundwater recharge and strengthen long-term water security. Under the Jaladhara Jalaharathi programme, implemented through convergence, the district undertook the restoration of traditional minor irrigation tanks and their feeder channels not merely to improve surface storage, but to revive natural recharge systems that replenish groundwater aquifers. The district completed 8,973 water conservation works, including the rejuvenation of 6,424 Minor Irrigation tanks and 2,549 feeder channels, generating 1.28 crore person-days of employment while creating durable groundwater recharge assets. Large-scale desilting and restoration removed nearly 109.9 lakh cubic metres of silt, cleared 82.48 lakh square metres of vegetation, and restored more than 2,090 kilometres of feeder channels, allowing rainwater to flow freely into tanks and recharge zones instead of being lost as runoff. The interventions are expected to substantially improve groundwater availability across the district. The rejuvenated tank system is projected to create an additional storage potential of 0.70 TMC, while the restored feeder channels and tanks together are expected to contribute nearly 0.60 TMC of groundwater recharge, enhancing aquifer replenishment and improving the resilience of local water resources against recurring dry spells. Recognising the importance of targeted groundwater management, the district prioritised 193 groundwater-deficit villages, where restoration works covered 596 feeder channels and 1,767 Minor Irrigation tanks. In addition, 94 cascade tank systems were rejuvenated to restore the natural hydrological connectivity between water bodies, improving infiltration and groundwater recharge across entire catchments. The success of Vizianagaram demonstrates that sustainable groundwater management extends beyond engineering interventions, it depends on active public participation. Farmers, Gram Panchayats, local communities, frontline workers and district administration collectively revived traditional water bodies that had gradually lost their recharge capacity over time. Their participation reflects the spirit of Jan Bhagidari, transforming water conservation into a community-led movement. As India continues the Jal Sanchay Jan Bhagidari: Catch the Rain campaign, Vizianagaram stands as an inspiring model of how reviving traditional water bodies can replenish groundwater, improve climate resilience and secure water resources for future generations. Echoing the Prime Minister's call to "Catch the Rain, where it falls, when it falls," the district has demonstrated that every restored tank, every rejuvenated feeder channel and every participating citizen contributes to building a water-secure India. **** ND/HM (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2292604) आगंतुक पटल  : 128 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu Ministry of Jal Shakti Jan Bhagidari Powers Groundwater Revival in Vizianagaram under Jal Sanchay Jan Bhagidari: Catch the Rain प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: 101 crore citizens now covered under India's social security net as recognised by ILO, says Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Labour & Employment 101 crore citizens now covered under India's social security net as recognised by ILO, says Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya Essential to have a balanced development model that advances workers’ welfare as well as employers’ interests, says Union Minister, Dr. Mandaviya Employment generated per percentage point of GDP growth has risen from 0.008 per cent twelve years ago to 1.11 per cent today: Dr Mandaviya Well-run private hospitals could be designated as ESIC facilities, states Union Minister ILO Representative congratulates India on giving social protection to over one billion citizens प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                31 JUL 2026 1:47PM by PIB Delhi India's social protection systems now cover about 101 crore people, or over 68 per cent of the population, Dr Mansukh Mandaviya, Union Minister for Labour & Employment and Youth Affairs & Sports, said at the 4th Global Industrial Relations Summit in New Delhi today. This figure, the Minister said, had been highlighted by the International Labour Organization (ILO) the BRICS Labour Ministers' Meeting in Hyderabad last week, testifying to a global recognition of India’s social security coverage. The Summit is organised by the All India Organisation of Employers (AIOE) in association with Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FICCI) and ILO. Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya said that harmonious industrial relations require continuous coordination among governments, industry, employers, workers and trade unions to ensure that economic development and employment generation progress together. Stressing that industrialisation is essential for national development as it drives employment creation, the Union Minister also underlined the growing importance of self-help groups and cooperative models, particularly women-led initiatives, in expanding livelihood opportunities, strengthening the economy and promoting women's empowerment. “It is essential to have a balanced development model that advances the welfare and social security of workers, as well as ensure ease of doing business for employers,” he stated. Dr. Mandaviya underlined that under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, sustained economic growth, supported by stable taxation, rising savings, higher purchasing power and increased manufacturing, has created a virtuous cycle of development and employment. Citing improving employment elasticity, he said that every one per cent increase in GDP is generating 1.11 per cent employment growth, as compared to 0.008 per cent growth in employment seen twelve years ago. Dr. Mandaviya also indicated that the Employees’ State Insurance Corporation (ESIC) need not remain the sole provider of care under its own scheme. Well-run private hospitals could be designated as ESIC facilities, he said, describing upcoming reform of the corporation. He also pointed to the Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation’s (EPFO) move to fully digital claims and automatic transfer of accounts on a single UAN, with UPI-based withdrawal under consideration. Ms Michiko Miyamoto, Director ILO DWT for South Asia and Country Office for India, congratulated India on the expansion of its social security coverage, noting that according to ILO estimate, the country had crossed one billion people covered by at least one social protection criterion. This achievement, she underscored, would play a key role in propelling India’s economic growth in the days ahead. A souvenir, marking the two-day Summit, was also released by the Union Minister Dr. Mandaviya, along with other dignitaries. ***** Rini Choudhury (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2292305) आगंतुक पटल  : 313 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: हिन्दी , Gujarati , Tamil , Kannada , Malayalam Ministry of Labour & Employment 101 crore citizens now covered under India's social security net as recognised by ILO, says Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya Essential to have a balanced development model that advances workers’ welfare as well as employers’ interests, says Union Minister, Dr. Mandaviya Employment generated per percentage point of GDP growth has risen from 0.008 per cent twelve years ago to 1.11 per cent today: Dr Mandaviya Well-run private hospitals could be designated as ESIC facilities, states Union Minister ILO Representative congratulates India on giving social protection to over one billion citizens प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: AI-based tool Legal Research Analysis Assistant (LegRAA) has been developed by the Artificial Intelligence Division of NIC and Centre of Excellence for eCourts
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Law and Justice AI-based tool Legal Research Analysis Assistant (LegRAA) has been developed by the Artificial Intelligence Division of NIC and Centre of Excellence for eCourts प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                31 JUL 2026 1:30PM by PIB Delhi The eCourts Mission Mode Project, under the National e-Governance Plan, is being implemented by Department of Justice in coordination with eCommittee, Supreme Court of India. Under the Phase-III of the Project, there is a provision for adoption of emerging technologies, including Artificial Intelligence (AI) to enhance judicial efficiency, for which an amount of ₹53.57 crore has been earmarked under the Future Technological Advancements component. As per the information provided by eCommittee, Supreme Court of India, an AI-based tool Legal Research Analysis Assistant (LegRAA) has been developed by the Artificial Intelligence Division of NIC and the Centre of Excellence for eCourts (CoEE), NIC to assist Hon'ble Judges in legal research and document analysis. Another AI-based tool, Digital Courts 2.1 has been developed by the Centre of Excellence for eCourts (CoEE), NIC, Pune, as an integrated digital case management platform. It provides a single-window interface for case-related information and incorporates AI-enabled features such as voice-to-text transcription and translation to assist Hon'ble Judges and Judicial Officers in dictation of orders and judgments. Both the tools are in pilot testing phase. The operational framework governing the deployment and future use of AI-based solutions, is decided, in accordance with the Rules of Business and the policies of Supreme Court of India and respective High Courts. This information was given by MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) OF THE MINISTRY OF LAW AND JUSTICE; AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PARLIAMENTARY AFFAIRS Shri Arjun Ram Meghwal in a written reply to a question in Lok Sabha today. *** Samrat/Pranab/Sagar (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2292285) आगंतुक पटल  : 230 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी , Tamil Ministry of Law and Justice AI-based tool Legal Research Analysis Assistant (LegRAA) has been developed by the Artificial Intelligence Division of NIC and Centre of Excellence for eCourts प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: Designing Innovative Solutions for Holistic Access to Justice (DISHA) 2.0 Scheme aims at leveraging technology to develop and enhance the outreach of people friendly solution platforms for legal services
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Law and Justice Designing Innovative Solutions for Holistic Access to Justice (DISHA) 2.0 Scheme aims at leveraging technology to develop and enhance the outreach of people friendly solution platforms for legal services DISHA 2.0 includes four components viz. Tele-Law: Reaching the Unreached (free pre litigation advice to all); Nyaya Bandhu (Pro-Bono legal Services) Programme; Legal Literacy and Legal Awareness Programme and VIDHI (Vision for Integrated Delivery of Harmonized Legal Initiatives)-Sanjeevani. प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                31 JUL 2026 1:29PM by PIB Delhi The Designing Innovative Solutions for Holistic Access to Justice (DISHA) 2.0 Scheme is a Central Sector Scheme for pan India implementation, including all the districts of Gujarat, for the period of 2026-31. DISHA 2.0 aims at leveraging technology to develop and enhance the outreach of people friendly solution platforms for legal services. It includes four components viz. Tele-Law: Reaching the Unreached (free pre litigation advice to all); Nyaya Bandhu (Pro-Bono legal Services) Programme; Legal Literacy and Legal Awareness Programme and VIDHI (Vision for Integrated Delivery of Harmonized Legal Initiatives)-Sanjeevani. The Monitoring of the progress of the Scheme is envisaged through VIDHI- Sanjeevani, a Centralized Integrated Dashboard apart from regular review meetings, field visits, and direct feedback by way of regional workshops and through a dedicated Programme Management Unit (PMU). title: To safeguard the rights of depositor/members of multi-State Cooperative Societies, various measures have been introduced through Multi-State Cooperative Societies (MSCS) (Amendment) Act & Rules, 2023
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Law and Justice To safeguard the rights of depositor/members of multi-State Cooperative Societies, various measures have been introduced through Multi-State Cooperative Societies (MSCS) (Amendment) Act & Rules, 2023 प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                31 JUL 2026 1:28PM by PIB Delhi Cooperative Societies registered under the provisions of the Multi-State Cooperative Societies (MSCS) Act, 2002, function as autonomous cooperative organisations and are accountable to their members. The MSCS Act, 2002 provides for provisions related to inquiry, inspection, winding up of societies, appointment of liquidators, offences, penalties and cognizance of offences. Whenever a complaint discloses the commission of cognizable offences such as fraud, cheating or criminal breach of trust under the applicable laws, the matter is referred to the concerned State Police, Economic Offences Wing (EOW), Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) or other competent investigating agencies, as the case may be, for investigation and prosecution in accordance with law. Recovery of the assets and realization of dues of societies under liquidation are undertaken by the Liquidator in accordance with the provisions of MSCS Act, 2002 and the applicable rules. Investigation and prosecution in criminal matters are undertaken by the competent investigating agencies and courts under the applicable criminal laws. The Office of the Central Registrar extends necessary cooperation by furnishing records, documents and other information whenever sought by the investigating agencies or courts. To safeguard the rights of depositor/members of multi-State Cooperative Societies, various measures have been introduced through Multi-State Cooperative Societies (MSCS) (Amendment) Act & Rules, 2023, including: Co-operative Ombudsman has been appointed by Central Government to provide a mechanism to address grievances of members and Information Officer has been appointment by multi-State cooperative societies to improve transparency. Audit and accounting framework has been strengthened through introduction of concurrent audit, determination of uniform accounting and auditing standards and laying of audit reports of Apex multi-State cooperative societies in the Parliament. Measures to improve governance and transparency, including disclosure of non-unanimous Board decisions in annual reports, additional grounds for disqualification of directors and restrictions on directors from participating in matters where they or their relatives have a conflict of interest have been introduced. Prudential norms (liquidity, exposure, etc.) for multi-State Cooperative Societies engaged in the business of thrift and credit have been determined and provisions relating to investment of funds to ensure safer investments have been redefined. Regulatory oversight has been strengthened by empowering the Central Registrar to conduct inquiry into fraudulent or unlawful functioning. Provision has been introduced for winding up of societies where registration was obtained through fraud or misrepresentation, after following due process. Measures have been introduced to protect the collective interests of societies, including increasing the minimum period of expulsion of expelled members from one year to three years. This information was given by MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) OF THE MINISTRY OF LAW AND JUSTICE; AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PARLIAMENTARY AFFAIRS Shri Arjun Ram Meghwal in a written reply to a question in Lok Sabha today. *** Samrat/Pranab/Sagar (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2292281) आगंतुक पटल  : 124 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी , Tamil Ministry of Law and Justice To safeguard the rights of depositor/members of multi-State Cooperative Societies, various measures have been introduced through Multi-State Cooperative Societies (MSCS) (Amendment) Act & Rules, 2023 प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: e-Courts Mission Mode Project is being implemented in a phased manner across the country with objective of strengthening use of Information and Communication Technology (ICT) in the judicial system
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Law and Justice e-Courts Mission Mode Project is being implemented in a phased manner across the country with objective of strengthening use of Information and Communication Technology (ICT) in the judicial system प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                31 JUL 2026 1:27PM by PIB Delhi The e-Courts Mission Mode Project is being implemented in a phased manner across the country with the objective of strengthening the use of Information and Communication Technology (ICT) in the judicial system. Various ICT-enabled initiatives, including the Case Information System (CIS) 4.0, e-Filing, e Payments, Video Conferencing, Virtual Courts, Digital Case Records, National Judicial Data Grid (NJDG), Interoperable Criminal Justice System (ICJS), eSewa Kendras, National Service and Tracking of Electronic Processes (NSTEP), the eCourts Services Portal and Mobile App, and other citizen-centric digital services, have been implemented across the High Courts and District Courts in a phased manner. The e-Filing system is an end-to-end digital platform for the online filing of cases, written statements, replies and other related applications. As on 30.06.2026, the Rules for e-Filing have been implemented in 25 High Courts, including the High Court of Uttarakhand and the District Courts under its jurisdiction. As on 30.06.2026, a total of 1.25 crore cases have been filed through the e-Filing system across the country. The details of cases filed through the e-Filing system, High Court-wise and District-wise, is placed at Annexure-I. (c): In the State of Uttarakhand, a total of 1.17 lakh cases have been filed through the e- Filing system before District Courts, including 356 cases efiled before the High Court of Uttarakhand. The District-wise details of cases filed through the e-Filing system in Uttarakhand, as received from the High Court of Uttarakhand, is placed at Annexure-II. To create awareness and promote adoption of the e-Filing system across the country, the eCommittee, Supreme Court of India, in coordination with the High Courts, has undertaken training programmes, capacity-building workshops and orientation sessions for Judicial Officers, court staff, advocates and other stakeholders through the State Judicial Academies and the respective High Courts. User manuals, Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), FAQs and video tutorials have also been prepared and disseminated to facilitate effective use of the e-Filing system. Further, eSewa Kendras have been established across the country to assist litigants and advocates in registration on the e-Filing portal, scanning and uploading of petitions and supporting documents, online payment of court fees and availing other services relating to e-Filing, thereby promoting awareness and facilitating wider adoption of the e-Filing system. This information was given by MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) OF THE MINISTRY OF LAW AND JUSTICE; AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PARLIAMENTARY AFFAIRS Shri Arjun Ram Meghwal in a written reply to a question in Lok Sabha today. *** Samrat/Pranab/Sagar Annexure-I STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY OF LOK SABHA UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2273 FOR 31.07.2026 REGARDING INFORMATION AND COMMUNICATION TECHNOLOGY IN INDIAN COURTS Details of number of cases e-filed in High Courts and District Courts till 30.06.2026 : S. title: Geological Survey of India Gets Its First Woman Director General
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Mines Geological Survey of India Gets Its First Woman Director General Smt. Varsha Ashok Aglawe Assumes Charge as the 54th Director General of Geological Survey of India प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                31 JUL 2026 8:09PM by PIB Delhi Smt. Varsha Ashok Aglawe has assumed charge as the 54th Director General of the Geological Survey of India (GSI), becoming the first woman to head India's premier geoscientific organisation in its 176-year history. She succeeds Shri Asit Saha, who served as Director General from 27 th July 2024 to 31 st July 2026. A distinguished geoscientist with more than three decades of professional experience, Smt. Aglawe joined GSI in 1992 after serving with the Indian Bureau of Mines. During her career, she has held several important scientific and administrative positions in GSI's Central, Northern and Eastern Regions, besides serving at Central Headquarters. Prior to assuming the present office, she was Additional Director General & Head of Department, Eastern Region, Kolkata. An expert in palaeontology and palynology, Smt. Aglawe has made significant contributions to the study of the Late Cretaceous–Palaeocene sediments, K-T boundary, and Satpura-Gondwana basins. She reported the Salbardi–Ghorpend area as a new dinosaur nesting site in Central India, contributed to international research and participated in collaborative palaeontological studies with the University of Michigan Museum of Paleontology, USA. She also represented GSI as a member of the Indian delegation to PDAC 2023 in Toronto, Canada. Besides her scientific contributions, she has played an important role in strengthening GSI's institutional capabilities, including establishing a state-of-the-art Palynology Laboratory at the Northern Region office in Lucknow and leading multidisciplinary geoscientific programmes across the country. On assuming office, Smt. Aglawe reaffirmed GSI's commitment to aligning its programmes with the Government of India's priorities in critical mineral exploration and mineral security. She emphasized accelerating exploration of deep-seated and concealed mineral deposits through advanced geophysical investigations, fast-tracked exploration programmes and strengthened laboratory infrastructure. She also highlighted the need to expand offshore mineral exploration, promote cutting-edge geoscientific research, strengthen public-good geoscience programmes such as natural hazard studies and glaciology, and enhance scientific publications and capacity building for young geoscientists. Expressing confidence in GSI's scientific expertise and expanding technological capabilities, she said the organisation is well positioned to meet the nation's growing demand for critical and strategic minerals while contributing to sustainable resource development through geoscientific excellence and innovation. *** PKMV (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2292720) आगंतुक पटल  : 81 Ministry of Mines Geological Survey of India Gets Its First Woman Director General Smt.
