title: Cabinet approves 'Pradhan Mantri Surya Sarovar Yojana (PM-SSY)' for Development of Floating Solar Photovoltaic Projects with Energy Storage Systems with a total outlay of Rs.5,070 crore
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of New and Renewable Energy Cabinet approves 'Pradhan Mantri Surya Sarovar Yojana (PM-SSY)' for Development of Floating Solar Photovoltaic Projects with Energy Storage Systems with a total outlay of Rs.5,070 crore प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                31 JUL 2026 4:28PM by PIB Delhi The Union Cabinet chaired by the Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi today approved the 'Pradhan Mantri Surya Sarovar Yojana (PM-SSY)’, a Scheme for the development of Floating Solar Photovoltaic (FSPV) Projects with Energy Storage Systems (ESS) with a total outlay of Rs.5,070 crore. The scheme envisages the development of 5,000 MW of Floating Solar Photovoltaic projects with co-located Energy Storage Systems having a minimum storage capacity of two hours i.e.,10,000 MWh. The projects will be sanctioned during FY 2026-27 to FY 2030-31, with disbursement of financial support continuing up to FY 2032-33. The approval follows the recent assessment undertaken by the National Institute of Solar Energy (NISE), which has estimated a floating solar potential of approximately 102.18 GWp across reservoirs and other suitable inland water bodies in the country. Under the scheme, Central Financial Assistance (CFA) of Rs. One crore per MW will be provided for eligible Floating Solar Photovoltaic projects after successful commissioning. In addition, CFA of up to Rs.50 lakh per project will be available for undertaking feasibility studies, including bathymetry and hydrography assessments, environmental studies, and other preparatory activities required for de-risking the project development. All States and Union Territories will benefit through this scheme. The scheme would enhance the floating Solar PV capacity in the country by 5,000 MW, which is presently around 700 MW only. These projects would provide an opportunity to gainfully utilize existing reservoirs & industrial ponds, and eliminate competition for scarce land resources. The integration of an energy storage system will help strengthen grid reliability. The scheme would help in the reduction of around 10 million tonnes of CO₂ emissions annually. It would help in the generation of approximately 16,000–17,000 full-time equivalent employment opportunities across the project value chain. The scheme would also promote domestic manufacturing of floatation systems as well as the entire value chain of the projects, like PV cells, modules, energy storage systems, etc., and support the vision of Aatmanirbhar Bharat. The scheme will contribute to renewable energy capacity addition, support the achievement of national energy and climate objectives, and facilitate optimal utilisation of water resources while advancing the vision of Viksit Bharat. **** MJPS (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2292465) आगंतुक पटल  : 259 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी , Punjabi , Gujarati , Kannada , Malayalam Ministry of New and Renewable Energy Cabinet approves 'Pradhan Mantri Surya Sarovar Yojana (PM-SSY)' for Development of Floating Solar Photovoltaic Projects with Energy Storage Systems with a total outlay of Rs.5,070 crore प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: Union Minister of State Prof. S.P. Singh Baghel Releases “51 Stories of Panchayats Bringing Change for Good Governance” Compendium in New Delhi
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Panchayati Raj Union Minister of State Prof. S.P. Singh Baghel Releases “51 Stories of Panchayats Bringing Change for Good Governance” Compendium in New Delhi Compendium highlights Effective CPGRAMS Grievance Redressal by the Ministry of Panchayati Raj Strengthening Citizens Trust in Panchayats प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                31 JUL 2026 8:20PM by PIB Delhi Union Minister of State for Panchayati Raj and Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying, Prof. S. P. Singh Baghel, released a compendium titled “51 Stories of Panchayats Bringing Change for Good Governance” (51 कहानियां बदलाव की, पंचायत सुराज की), today in New Delhi . The occasion was graced by Shri Vivek Bharadwaj, Secretary, Ministry of Panchayati Raj along with other senior officers of the Ministry. Speaking on the occasion, Prof. Baghel said that the compilation would serve as a valuable source of learning and inspiration for all stakeholders associated with the Panchayati Raj system. He observed that every grievance resolved represents a meaningful step towards strengthening responsive, participatory and citizen-centric governance. Shri Vivek Bharadwaj said that, in line with the vision of the Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, Ministry of Panchayati Raj has accorded highest priority to timely redressal of public grievances through CPGRAMS. He added that sustained efforts to address grievances, including those from the remotest parts of the country, have helped strengthen a responsive and citizen-friendly grievance redressal mechanism while reinforcing public trust in institutions. Prepared by the Ministry of Panchayati Raj in collaboration with the Panchayati Raj Departments of various States, the compendium presents Fifty-One inspiring Case Studies of successful redressal of Public Grievances received on the Centralised Public Grievance Redress and Monitoring System (CPGRAMS). These stories demonstrate how timely and effective resolution of citizens’ concerns improves service delivery, strengthens accountability, enhances basic civic infrastructure and makes a tangible difference to people’s lives at the grassroots. *** AA (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2292728) आगंतुक पटल  : 22 Ministry of Panchayati Raj Union Minister of State Prof. S.P. title: Cabinet approves 'Samudra Manthan' (National Offshore Exploration Scheme) with an outlay of Rs.84,084 crore
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas Cabinet approves 'Samudra Manthan' (National Offshore Exploration Scheme) with an outlay of Rs.84,084 crore प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                31 JUL 2026 4:21PM by PIB Delhi The Union Cabinet chaired by the Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi has approved 'Samudra Manthan' – the National Offshore Exploration Scheme, a Central Sector Scheme of the Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas with an approved outlay of Rs.84,084 crore for implementation up to FY 2030–31. The Scheme translates the  Prime Minister's vision, articulated from the Red Fort on Independence Day 2025, of a modern-day Samudra Manthan to unlock India's vast offshore energy potential. It marks a landmark step towards strengthening India's energy security, accelerating domestic exploration and production, promoting technological leadership, and advancing the vision of Viksit Bharat. The Scheme encompasses a comprehensive set of interventions across the offshore exploration value chain. It provides for large-scale acquisition, processing and interpretation of high-quality seismic data, accelerated deepwater and ultra-deepwater exploratory drilling, scientific drilling in frontier basins, development of common offshore production and evacuation infrastructure, and establishment of an integrated Oil & Gas Manufacturing and Services Zone. It also includes dedicated provisions for digital programme management, capacity building, technology adoption, stakeholder engagement and international outreach, creating an integrated ecosystem to accelerate offshore exploration and production in the country. Samudra Manthan is expected to catalyse reserve accretion of over 600 Million Metric Tons of Oil Equivalentv(MMTOE), substantially increase offshore exploration activity, promote higher domestic oil and gas production, generate large-scale employment, strengthen indigenous manufacturing under Make in India and Atmanirbhar Bharat, and foster a globally competitive ecosystem for offshore technologies and services. The Scheme is also expected to stimulate significant investments across the exploration and production value chain, creating long-term opportunities for industry, innovation and economic growth. As India progresses towards becoming a developed nation, Samudra Manthan represents a transformational national initiative that will unlock the country's offshore energy resources, strengthen long-term energy security, deepen technological capabilities, and create enduring value for the economy and future generations. Over the past decade, the Government has undertaken transformative reforms across the upstream sector, including opening almost the entire offshore acreage for exploration, modernising the legislative and contractual framework, and strengthening the National Data Repository. Building on these reforms, Samudra Manthan will usher in a new era of accelerated offshore exploration through strategic public investment, cutting-edge technologies and world-class infrastructure. **** MJPS (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2292454) आगंतुक पटल  : 473 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Malayalam , Urdu , हिन्दी , Punjabi , Gujarati , Tamil , Kannada Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas Cabinet approves 'Samudra Manthan' (National Offshore Exploration Scheme) with an outlay of Rs.84,084 crore प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: India's ethanol blended petrol programme balances food security, farmer welfare and energy security
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas India's ethanol blended petrol programme balances food security, farmer welfare and energy security Without ethanol blending, petrol would have cost around ₹125 per litre during the global oil price surge प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                31 JUL 2026 12:17PM by PIB Delhi The Ethanol Blended Petrol (EBP) Programme is a key national initiative to enhance India's energy security, reduce dependence on imported crude oil and support farmers while safeguarding food security. Certain recent claims have presented an incomplete and misleading picture of the programme. The following clarifications address these issues and set out the factual position. Claim: The Government sold FCI rice worth ₹37/kg to distilleries at ₹23/kg, causing a loss of ₹10,000 crore. The Government has also admitted that ethanol is more expensive than petrol, so E20 survives only because taxpayers subsidise it. No compromise on food security — ethanol never comes at the cost of the poor The allegation is not just misleading; it turns the truth on its head. Every food grain grain first serves the Public Distribution System (PDS), the National Food Security Act (NFSA), welfare schemes, and mandatory buffer stocks. Not a single grain procured at MSP is diverted to ethanol before India's food security is secured. Only the surplus, certified by the Department of Food & Public Distribution after every food security obligation has been met, is approved for ethanol production . What actually goes into the ethanol programme is the damaged grain, broken rice, and foodgrain unfit for human consumption—stocks that would otherwise rot in warehouses. This is not taking food away from the poor; it is turning waste into wealth, reducing imports, and putting more money into the hands of Indian farmers. And the programme is moving even further ahead. Through the Pradhan Mantri JI-VAN Yojana, India is rapidly expanding 2G (Second generation) ethanol from agricultural residue , reducing dependence on food grains altogether. The facts are clear: the Government protects every grain needed for food security first, and only then converts surplus and waste into clean energy. The claim isn't just wrong, it ignores the very safeguards that make India's ethanol programme one of the world's most responsible. Rice was not given special treatment The claim creates the impression that FCI rice was sold to ethanol producers at an unusually cheap price. That is simply not true. FCI rice is just one of several approved raw materials used to make ethanol and its price is fixed under the same government pricing framework as every other feedstock. Feedstock (ESY 2025-26) Ethanol price paid Maize ₹71.86/litre Sugarcane Juice/Syrup ₹65.61/litre Damaged Foodgrains ₹64.00/litre B-heavy Molasses ₹60.73/litre FCI Rice ₹60.32/litre C-heavy Molasses ₹57.97/litre The programme does not depend on rice. It uses whichever approved feedstock is available. In ESY 2023-24 , FCI rice contributed virtually nothing—just 0.02% of ethanol production. By ESY 2025-26 , its share increased to 24.64% only because surplus FCI stocks became available after all food security needs had been met . During the same period, maize's share declined from 42.6% to 35.96% , showing that producers simply switch between different feedstocks depending on availability. Ethanol is not built around cheap rice . It is built around a flexible mix of approved feedstocks , with FCI rice used only when certified surplus stocks are available after meeting every food security obligation. The real question isn't whether ethanol is cheaper — it's whether India is better protected The real question is this: What would Indians have paid if there had been no ethanol blending when global oil prices surged? When the Indian crude basket surged to around US$135 per barrel, petrol without ethanol blending was projected to cost around ₹125 per litre in Delhi. Instead, consumers paid ₹94.77 per litre because 20% of every litre was domestically produced ethanol, procured at stable, pre-agreed prices that were insulated from the global crude price spike. The result? Nearly ₹30 per litre in savings at the pump during the peak of the crisis. That is the real value of ethanol blending. It is not about being the cheapest fuel every day. It is about protecting Indian consumers from extreme volatility in global oil markets, strengthening India's energy security, and keeping more of the country's fuel bill within the Indian economy rather than sending it overseas. The results of the program speak for themselves. The EBP Program has already delivered: More than ₹1.97 lakh crore in foreign exchange savings; Substitution of over 316 lakh metric tonnes of crude oil imports; Reduction of more than 950 lakh metric tonnes of CO₂ emissions; and Over ₹1.66 lakh crore in payments to farmers and distillers, creating a stable domestic market for agricultural produce. The purpose of ethanol blending is to reduce India's dependence on imported crude oil, which still meets nearly 88% of our oil requirement. It is an insurance policy against global oil shocks and not a day-to-day price competition. Ethanol blending isn't a taxpayer subsidy. It's India's energy insurance and it has already delivered when the crisis hit. ******** TM (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2292225) आगंतुक पटल  : 692 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Khasi , Urdu , हिन्दी , Marathi , Bengali , Assamese , Gujarati , Tamil , Telugu , Kannada , Malayalam Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas India's ethanol blended petrol programme balances food security, farmer welfare and energy security Without ethanol blending, petrol would have cost around ₹125 per litre during the global oil price surge प्रविष्टि तिथि:

Feedstock (ESY 2025-26) Ethanol price paid Maize ₹71.86/litre Sugarcane Juice/Syrup ₹65.61/litre Damaged Foodgrains ₹64.00/litre B-heavy Molasses ₹60.73/litre FCI Rice ₹60.32/litre C-heavy Molasses ₹57.97/litre The programme does not depend on rice. It uses whichever approved feedstock is available. In ESY 2023-24 , FCI rice contributed virtually nothing—just 0.02% of ethanol production. By ESY 2025-26 , its share increased to 24.64% only because surplus FCI stocks became available after all food security needs had been met . During the same period, maize's share declined from 42.6% to 35.96% , showing that producers simply switch between different feedstocks depending on availability. Ethanol is not built around cheap rice . It is built around a flexible mix of approved feedstocks , with FCI rice used only when certified surplus stocks are available after meeting every food security obligation. The real question isn't whether ethanol is cheaper — it's whether India is better protected The real question is this: What would Indians have paid if there had been no ethanol blending when global oil prices surged? When the Indian crude basket surged to around US$135 per barrel, petrol without ethanol blending was projected to cost around ₹125 per litre in Delhi. Instead, consumers paid ₹94.77 per litre because 20% of every litre was domestically produced ethanol, procured at stable, pre-agreed prices that were insulated from the global crude price spike. The result? Nearly ₹30 per litre in savings at the pump during the peak of the crisis. That is the real value of ethanol blending. It is not about being the cheapest fuel every day. It is about protecting Indian consumers from extreme volatility in global oil markets, strengthening India's energy security, and keeping more of the country's fuel bill within the Indian economy rather than sending it overseas. The results of the program speak for themselves. The EBP Program has already delivered: More than ₹1.97 lakh crore in foreign exchange savings; Substitution of over 316 lakh metric tonnes of crude oil imports; Reduction of more than 950 lakh metric tonnes of CO₂ emissions; and Over ₹1.66 lakh crore in payments to farmers and distillers, creating a stable domestic market for agricultural produce. The purpose of ethanol blending is to reduce India's dependence on imported crude oil, which still meets nearly 88% of our oil requirement. It is an insurance policy against global oil shocks and not a day-to-day price competition. Ethanol blending isn't a taxpayer subsidy. It's India's energy insurance and it has already delivered when the crisis hit. ******** TM (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2292225)

title: Indian Railways Successfully Transports India's First Live Donor Heart by Train; Vande Bharat Express Enables Life-saving Mission from Surat to Ahmedabad
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Railways Indian Railways Successfully Transports India's First Live Donor Heart by Train; Vande Bharat Express Enables Life-saving Mission from Surat to Ahmedabad Exemplary Coordination Between Indian Railways, RPF, Gujarat Police and Medical Teams Demonstrates Railways' Expanding Role in Life-saving Healthcare Services प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                31 JUL 2026 5:20PM by PIB Delhi Indian Railways has achieved a historic milestone in the field of healthcare by successfully transporting a live donor heart by train for the first time in India. The life-saving organ was transported from Surat to Ahmedabad aboard Train No. 20901 Mumbai Central-Gandhinagar Capital Vande Bharat Express, ensuring its safe and timely arrival for transplantation at the U.N. Mehta Institute of Cardiology & Research Centre, Ahmedabad. The landmark mission showcased the speed, punctuality and reliability of Vande Bharat Express while highlighting the growing role of Indian Railways in supporting critical healthcare services and emergency medical transportation. Given the highly time-sensitive nature of organ transplantation, the operation required meticulous planning and seamless coordination among Indian Railways, the Railway Protection Force (RPF), Gujarat State Police and medical teams. Every stage of the transportation was carefully synchronised to ensure that the donor heart reached the recipient hospital within the prescribed viability window. A dedicated Green Corridor was created from Platform No. 1 of Ahmedabad Railway Station to the U.N. Mehta Institute of Cardiology & Research Centre by the Railway Protection Force and Gujarat State Police, enabling uninterrupted movement of the donor heart and ensuring that the transplant procedure could commence without delay. Speaking on the occasion, Shri Ved Prakash, Divisional Railway Manager, Ahmedabad, said,"This is a moment of immense pride and satisfaction for Indian Railways. The successful transportation of a live donor heart from Surat to Ahmedabad through Vande Bharat Express demonstrates our commitment to serving society beyond conventional passenger and freight transportation. In such life-saving missions, every minute is crucial. The excellent coordination among Indian Railways, RPF, Gujarat State Police and the medical teams ensured the success of this mission. Contributing towards saving a human life is not only our responsibility but also our highest duty towards service and humanity." The successful mission further reinforces the capability of Vande Bharat Express to support time-critical operations through its high-speed connectivity, operational reliability and punctuality. It also demonstrates how modern railway infrastructure can play a crucial role in strengthening the country's emergency healthcare ecosystem. Indian Railways expressed its appreciation to all stakeholders, including the Railway Protection Force, Gujarat State Police, doctors, organ transplant coordinators and railway officials, whose coordinated efforts made this challenging mission a success. This historic achievement reaffirms Indian Railways' commitment to providing safe, reliable and efficient transportation services while extending its support to life-saving humanitarian initiatives and contributing to the nation's healthcare system. ***** Mahesh Kumar/ Dr. Nayan Solanki/ Ritu Raj/ Manik Sharma (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2292539) आगंतुक पटल  : 354 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: हिन्दी , Kannada , Malayalam Ministry of Railways Indian Railways Successfully Transports India's First Live Donor Heart by Train; Vande Bharat Express Enables Life-saving Mission from Surat to Ahmedabad Exemplary Coordination Between Indian Railways, RPF, Gujarat Police and Medical Teams Demonstrates Railways' Expanding Role in Life-saving Healthcare Services प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: EXPANSION OF SARAS AAJEEVIKA AND MARKET ACCESS FOR RURAL WOMEN SHGS
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Rural Development EXPANSION OF SARAS AAJEEVIKA AND MARKET ACCESS FOR RURAL WOMEN SHGS प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                31 JUL 2026 5:20PM by PIB Delhi Under the Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana–National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM), the Ministry of Rural Development is strengthening market access for Self Help Groups (SHGs) products through retail stores, organisation of SARAS Melas and promotion of SHG products through the digital marketing platform across the country, including Rajasthan. As per the Ministry’s guidelines all State Rural Livelihoods Missions (SRLMs), including Rajasthan, may organize at least two SARAS Fairs annually in their respective States. The Rajasthan State Rural Livelihoods Mission (Rajeevika) has identified locations for organizing SARAS Melas and establishing retail outlets under the State SHG brand, based on market potential and local requirements, to enhance market access for SHG products. Under DAY-NRLM, the Ministry of Rural Development supports women SHGs, including those from small towns, rural and aspirational districts of Rajasthan, through a range of marketing interventions. These include development of State level SHG brands, training on packaging, labelling and product standardization, participation in SARAS Melas, exhibitions and trade fairs. The SHGs are also onboarded on eSARAS and on other e-commerce platforms. The capacity building initiative focuses on digital marketing and facilitation of participation in selected business fairs and exhibitions to promote export ready SHG products. The National Institute of Rural Development and Panchayati Raj regularly conducts capacity building and skill development programmes to support SHG members on product development, branding, packaging, quality improvement, digital marketing, enterprise management, export procedures and documentation, and market readiness to strengthen their access to domestic and international markets. This information was given by the Minister of State for Rural Development DR. CHANDRA SEKHAR PEMMASANI in a written reply in Rajya Sabha today. ***** RC/PU (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2292537) आगंतुक पटल  : 135 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी Ministry of Rural Development EXPANSION OF SARAS AAJEEVIKA AND MARKET ACCESS FOR RURAL WOMEN SHGS प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: FUNDS UNDER VB-G RAM G
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Rural Development FUNDS UNDER VB-G RAM G प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                31 JUL 2026 5:19PM by PIB Delhi The Viksit Bharat–Guarantee for Rozgar and Aajeevika Mission (Gramin) (VB-G RAM G) Act, 2025 has come into force with effect from 1st July, 2026 in rural areas of the entire country. All States and UTs have notified the VB G RAM G Scheme and have started implementing the same. The State/UT-wise details of interim allocation made, mother sanctions issued under the VB-G RAM G Scheme since its commencement on 01.07.2026 are given at Annexure . There are no dues pertaining to any of the States/UTs are pending under Viksit Bharat–Guarantee for Rozgar and Aajeevika Mission (Gramin) (VB-G RAM G) Scheme as on date. The Government continuously monitors the implementation of the VB-G RAM G Scheme through the Management Information System (MIS), regular review meetings and other appropriate mechanisms. Prompt sanction of interim allocation and issuance of mother sanction has enabled the States/UTs to facilitate timely payment of wages under VB G RAM G. The VB-G RAM G Act, 2025 provides a statutory framework for timely and effective implementation of the Scheme. The budgetary allocation of ₹ 95,692.31 made for the VB-G RAM G Scheme, for FY-2026-27 (for the period from 01.07.2026 to 31.03.2027) is among the largest ever allocation made at the Budget Estimate Stage for any rural employment scheme in the history of the country. Further a normative allocation of ₹ 95,692.31 crore has already been done among States/UTs and mother sanctions amounting to ₹ 25,844.97, as first installment, have also been issued. This will help in providing statutory guarantee of one hundred and twenty-five days of wage employment to every household whose adult members volunteer to undertake unskilled manual work. States/UTs have also been requested to expeditiously utilize the sanctioned fund and ensure timely payment of wages to the workers. title: PROGRESS OF PRADHAN MANTRI AWAS YOJANA-GRAMIN (PMAY-G)
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Rural Development PROGRESS OF PRADHAN MANTRI AWAS YOJANA-GRAMIN (PMAY-G) प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                31 JUL 2026 5:17PM by PIB Delhi A total of 33.54 lakh houses have been sanctioned and 35.54 lakh houses (inclusive of sanctions issued in previous years) have been completed under PMAY-G for the year 2025-26 upto June 2026. In the State of Jharkhand, 1.48 lakh houses have been sanctioned and 0.68 lakh houses have been completed under PMAY-G during this period. As on date, a cumulative target of 4.18 crore houses have been allocated under the PMAY-G to the States and Union Territories (UTs) against which 3.92 crore houses have been sanctioned, 3.11 crore houses completed and 1.06 crore houses are remaining to be completed against allocated targets. State-wise/Union Territory-wise details of balance completion against targets, including State of Jharkhand are provided in Annexure I . The State Governments/UT Administrations are the primary implementing authorities at the ground level. As reported by the States/UTs, the major reasons for delays in completion include cases of unwillingness of beneficiaries, permanent migration, disputed succession of deceased beneficiaries, delay in allotment of land to landless beneficiaries by the States/UTs, the delay in updation of credit confirmation from State IFMIS and at times General/Assembly/ Panchayat elections and unavailability of building materials. The Ministry regularly reviews the progress reported by the States/UTs and takes up such implementation issues with them for timely resolution. Under PMAY-G, the beneficiaries are provided financial assistance of ₹1.20 lakh in plain areas and ₹1.30 lakh in the North-Eastern Region States and 2 Hill States (Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand) and Union Territories of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh. In addition to the Unit Assistance provided under the scheme, financial assistance of ₹12,000 is extended for the construction of toilets through convergence with the Swachh Bharat Mission-Gramin (SBM-G). Further, there is a provision for providing prescribed person-days of unskilled wage employment within the approved scheme parameters, at prevailing wage rates to each PMAY-G beneficiary for the construction of their house through convergence with MGNREGS/ VB G-RAM G. PMAY-G households are also provided with piped drinking water through convergence with the Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) and Har Ghar Nal Se Jal (HGNSJ) of the Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation, Ministry of Jal Shakti, or other similar schemes. In addition, beneficiaries are supported with electricity connection through relevant schemes implemented by the Ministry of Power, State Governments, or UT Administrations, and are provided Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) connections under the Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana (PMUY) of the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas or other relevant schemes. Convergence under PMAY-G also includes the inclusion of women members of beneficiary households in Self-Help Groups (SHGs), thereby promoting their social and economic empowerment. At the national level, as on date, a total of 3.10 crore houses have been provided with toilets, 2.45 crore houses with water connections, 3.08 crore houses with electricity connections, 2.91 crore houses with LPG connections, and 1.35 crore beneficiary households have been associated with Self-Help Groups (SHGs). The approved duration of phase-2 of PMAY-G for completing additional 2 crore houses is March 2029. In this regard to complete the pending 1.06 crore houses, number of steps have been taken by the Government to accelerate construction of houses in all States/UTs including Jharkhand, to achieve the targets under PMAY-G. Convergence under PMAY-G also includes the inclusion of women members of beneficiary households in Self-Help Groups (SHGs), thereby promoting their social and economic empowerment. At the national level, as on date, a total of 3.10 crore houses have been provided with toilets, 2.45 crore houses with water connections, 3.08 crore houses with electricity connections, 2.91 crore houses with LPG connections, and 1.35 crore beneficiary households have been associated with Self-Help Groups (SHGs). The approved duration of phase-2 of PMAY-G for completing additional 2 crore houses is March 2029. In this regard to complete the pending 1.06 crore houses, number of steps have been taken by the Government to accelerate construction of houses in all States/UTs including Jharkhand, to achieve the targets under PMAY-G. These include timely allocation of targets and release of adequate funds to the States/UTs, Regular review of progress, Monitoring and supervision of the scheme on a Dashboard, Regular Workshops by the Ministry with the States/UTs, Rural Mason Training program, etc. Annexure -I State-wise/Union Territory-wise details of progress under PMAY-G and pending houses against targets since inception of the scheme: #SNo Name of the State/UT Target allocated by Ministry Houses sanctioned by States/UTs Houses Completed Balance completion against targets 1 Arunachal Pradesh 35,937 35,591 35,591 346 2 Assam 29,62,945 29,09,060 22,94,143 6,68,802 3 Bihar 50,12,752 49,09,826 41,94,392 8,18,360 4 Chhattisgarh 26,42,224 24,51,591 20,28,201 6,14,023 5 Goa 257 254 243 14 6 Gujarat 8,39,116 8,29,442 7,19,165 1,19,951 7 Haryana 1,06,460 76,472 41,269 65,191 8 Himachal Pradesh 1,08,389 1,03,082 69,358 39,031 9 Jammu And Kashmir 3,41,644 3,35,360 3,26,710 14,934 10 Jharkhand 20,12,107 19,37,948 16,41,493 3,70,614 11 Kerala 1,13,404 86,014 40,789 72,615 12 Madhya Pradesh 57,74,572 54,16,056 43,57,001 14,17,571 13 Maharashtra 43,80,522 41,39,196 20,32,712 23,47,810 14 Manipur 1,13,550 1,06,812 56,932 56,618 15 Meghalaya 1,88,034 1,84,295 1,59,753 28,281 16 Mizoram 29,967 29,959 25,441 4,526 17 Nagaland 48,830 48,727 38,140 10,690 18 Odisha 28,28,739 28,06,697 25,48,674 2,80,065 19 Punjab 1,13,911 1,04,723 55,563 58,348 20 Rajasthan 24,93,546 24,32,017 20,31,138 4,62,408 21 Sikkim 1,399 1,397 1,393 6 22 Tamil Nadu 9,57,825 7,34,017 6,72,338 2,85,487 23 Tripura 3,76,913 3,76,174 3,73,940 2,973 24 Uttar Pradesh 42,77,493 36,55,817 36,42,983 6,34,510 25 Uttarakhand 69,755 68,936 68,242 1,513 26 West Bengal 46,69,423 45,69,031 34,20,433 12,48,990 27 Andaman And Nicobar 3,424 2,591 1,512 1,912 28 Dadra And Nagar Haveli 11,364 10,282 6,875 4,489 29 Daman And Diu 158 158 54 104 30 Lakshadweep 45 45 45 -                 31 JUL 2026 5:16PM by PIB Delhi Since inception, a total of 1,98,011 roads covering 8,55,980.33 km and 12,576 bridges have been sanctioned out of which 1,85,651 roads covering 7,96,940.94 km and 10,833 bridges have been constructed across the country under various verticals of the PMGSY. The vertical-wise details are given below:- Vertical Details Constructed No. of Roads Road Length (in km) No. of Bridges PMGSY-I 1,63,851 6,25,488.10 7,257 PMGSY-II 6,634 49,130.23 750 RCPLWEA 1,086 9,961.60 586 PMGSY III 13,408 1,08,970.37 2,240 PM-JANMAN 672 3,041.95 0 PMGSY-IV 0 348.69 0 Total: 1,85,651 7,96,940.94 10,833 The State wise, District-wise and Parliamentary Constituency wise details of rural road projects and the stages of construction under various verticals of PMGSY may be accessed at the programme website https://pmgsy.dord.gov.in/dbweb. Under the road connectivity component of Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan (PM-JANMAN), a total of 8000 km of road length, including bridges, is targeted to be constructed for providing all-weather connectivity to the unconnected Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups inhabited habitations across the country. The timeline for completion of PM-JANMAN is March 2028. Since inception, under PM-JANMAN,an amount of Rs. 1218 crore has been released against allocation of Rs. 4708 crore and the expenditure as on 26.07.2026 is Rs. 1542 crore. Vibrant Villages Programme–I (VVP-I) is a Centrally Sponsored initiative of the Government of India aimed at improving infrastructure and quality of life in strategically important villages along the northern international border. Under VVP-I, 113 roads covering 1,085 Km and 35 bridges have been sanctioned to connect 137 habitations. As on 26.7.2026, 10 roads covering 248 Km have been completed and an amount of Rs.996.72 crores have been released. The State wise details of the projects sanctioned, completed and balance under VVP-I are given at Annexure-I. VVP-II is being implemented in convergence with PMGSY IV. The Ministry had issued new technology initiatives guidelines in 2013 in order to use locally, marginally available materials/non-conventional materials/new materials in road construction. In order to encourage new materials in road construction, States/UTs were required to adopt new technologies in 15% of total proposals (10% using IRC mainstreaming technologies and 5% IRC accredited technologies). In order to promote and disseminate large scale adoption of New/Green Technologies in rural roads in a more systematic manner, the Ministry has revised these guidelines and brought out “Vision Document on New Technology Initiatives & Guidelines-2022” which requires the State Governments to propose minimum 50% of total length of annual proposals under New/ Green Technologies such as cement stabilization, lime stabilization, cold mix, waste plastics, cell-filled concrete, paneled cement-concrete pavement and fly ash. Two interventions, namely, PMGSY-II for up-gradation of 50,000 km of the existing rural roads and PMGSY-III for consolidation of 1, 25,000 km Through Routes and Major Rural Links connecting habitations, inter-alia , to Gramin Agricultural Markets (GrAMs), Higher Secondary Schools and Hospitals, were added under the ambit of PMGSY to integrate the PMGSY roads to government facilities and institutions. Under PMGSY-III, a total of 6,96,620 facility centres have been connected with habitations, out of which 1,38,637 are agricultural markets, 1,46,784 are educational centres, 82,806 are medical centres and 3,28,393 are connected to transportation hubs. As per the PMGSY guidelines, the contractors who constructed the road projects are required to provide maintenance during the five-year Defect Liability Period (DLP) for roads and bridges, post the construction. During the DLP, they are responsible for rectifying defects and maintain the road as per the prescribed standards. To ensure compliance with this maintenance obligation, the following measures have been implemented: (i) Mandatory contractual provision: The five-year maintenance obligation forms an integral part of the contract agreement executed with the contractor. (ii) Performance-Based Maintenance Contract (PBMC): Maintenance during the Defect Liability Period is carried out through a Performance-Based Maintenance Contract, under which payments are linked to the prescribed service levels and road condition. (iii) Regular inspections: Roads are inspected periodically by Programme Implementation Units (PIUs) and State Quality Monitors (SQMs) to assess compliance with prescribed maintenance standards and identify defects requiring rectification. (iv) Digital monitoring through eMARG: The States/UTs have been advised to adopt the eMARG (Electronic Maintenance of Rural Roads) platform for digital monitoring of maintenance activities, recording inspections, reporting defects, tracking rectification, and processing maintenance payments. (v) Quality monitoring mechanism: PMGSY follows a three-tier quality monitoring system comprising inspections by PIUs, State Quality Monitors (SQMs), and National Quality Monitors (NQMs) to ensure that roads are maintained in accordance with the prescribed standards. (vi) Corrective action and contractual remedies: Contractors are required to rectify defects noticed during the DLP within the stipulated time. Failure to do so attracts action in accordance with the contract provisions, including withholding of maintenance payments, forfeiture of performance security, execution of repairs at the contractor's risk and cost, and other contractual remedies. These measures are intended to ensure that rural roads constructed under PMGSY are adequately maintained during the mandatory five-year Defect Liability Period, thereby, preserving their quality, serviceability and longevity. title: EMPLOYMENT GUARANTEE AND LIVELIHOOD SUPPORT UNDER VB-G RAM G
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Rural Development EMPLOYMENT GUARANTEE AND LIVELIHOOD SUPPORT UNDER VB-G RAM G प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                31 JUL 2026 5:15PM by PIB Delhi The Viksit Bharat–Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) (VB-G RAM G) Act, 2025 has come into force with effect from 1st July, 2026 with the objective of enhancing livelihood security of rural households through a strengthened statutory framework for enhanced guaranteed wage employment of 125 days, creation of durable and productive rural assets, promotion of sustainable livelihoods and strengthening of rural infrastructure. The Act envisages a Whole-of-Government Approach by promoting convergence with other Central and State Government programmes and lays emphasis on Water-related Works, Core Rural Infrastructure, livelihood-related Infrastructure and works for the mitigation of extreme weather events, while encouraging technology-enabled planning, implementation, monitoring and transparency. As per sub-section (2) of section 22 of the Act, the fund sharing pattern between the Central Government and the State Governments shall be 90:10 for the North Eastern States, Himalayan States and Union territory (Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh and Jammu and Kashmir) and 60:40 for all other States and Union territories with legislature. For the current financial year 2026–27, a Central share provision of ₹95,692.31 crore has been made for the Scheme, representing the largest allocation ever for rural employment at the Budget Estimate Stage. With the inclusion of the corresponding estimated State share, the total programme outlay is likely to exceed ₹1.51 lakh crore, which is expected to significantly accelerate rural transformation, large-scale employment generation and income enhancement in rural areas. The VB-G RAM G Act, 2025 enhances the guaranteed employment from 100 days to 125 days in a financial year for every rural household whose adult members volunteer to do unskilled manual work. The Act further strengthens the statutory rights of workers by expressly providing for unemployment allowance where employment is not provided within the stipulated time and compensation for delay in payment of wages. It also provides for simplified mechanisms for registration and demand for employment. Further, wage payments under the Scheme are processed through the DBT-SPARSH platform, to facilitate timely, transparent and accountable transfer of wages directly into the bank accounts of workers. Further Gram Panchayat will continue to play important role in implementation of the scheme. The VB-G RAM G Act, 2025 provides a comprehensive institutional framework for monitoring, evaluation and grievance redressal to ensure effective implementation of the Scheme and timely delivery of benefits to eligible rural households, including vulnerable workers. The implementation of the Scheme is monitored through a technology-enabled Management Information System (MIS), periodic review meetings at various levels, social audits, inspections and other monitoring mechanisms prescribed under the Act. The Act also provides for a time-bound, multi-tier grievance redressal mechanism at the Block and District levels for receiving and disposing of grievances relating to implementation of the Scheme. In addition, the Ministry provides technical support, capacity building and handholding to the States/UTs from time to time to strengthen its effective implementation. These measures are aimed at ensuring transparency, accountability, efficient service delivery and effective implementation of the VB-G RAM G Scheme in accordance with the provisions of the VB-G RAM G Act, 2025. This information was given by the Minister of State for Rural Development SHRI KAMLESH PASWAN in a written reply in Rajya Sabha today. ***** RC/PU (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2292527) आगंतुक पटल  : 100 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी Ministry of Rural Development EMPLOYMENT GUARANTEE AND LIVELIHOOD SUPPORT UNDER VB-G RAM G प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: Dr. Jitendra Singh calls for connecting "Grassroots Innovators" with country's formal innovation ecosystem
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Science & Technology Dr. Jitendra Singh calls for connecting "Grassroots Innovators" with country's formal innovation ecosystem India’s Next Wave of Growth Will Emerge from Villages, Small Towns and Community Innovators: Dr. Jitendra Singh Grassroots Innovator Recognition Ceremony Honours 26 Innovators; Dr. Jitendra Singh Calls for National Innovation Pathway Local Solutions Must Evolve into National Enterprises to Realise Viksit Bharat: Dr. Jitendra Singh प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                31 JUL 2026 4:20PM by PIB Delhi Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science & Technology, Earth Sciences, and Minister of State for PMO, Personnel, Public Grievances, Pensions, Atomic Energy and Space, Dr. Jitendra Singh today called for connecting "Grassroots Innovators" with country's formal innovation ecosystem and said that India’s next wave of growth will emerge from villages, small towns and community innovators, not only from laboratories and large cities, asserting that grassroots innovations hold the key to building an Atmanirbhar Bharat and realising the vision of Viksit Bharat@2047. Calling for a seamless pathway to transform grassroots innovations into nationally scalable enterprises, he said innovation must move beyond recognition to scientific validation, technology translation, incubation and market adoption so that local solutions evolve into national assets capable of addressing India’s developmental priorities. Addressing the Grassroots Innovator Recognition Ceremony 2026 at the Rashtrapati Bhavan Cultural Centre, New Delhi, Dr. Jitendra Singh said the Government, under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, has transformed innovation into a nationwide movement by democratising access to science, technology and entrepreneurship. He said the Atal Innovation Mission (AIM) has expanded the innovation ecosystem beyond premier institutions and metropolitan centres, enabling talented innovators from rural, tribal, hilly, coastal, aspirational and remote regions to become active partners in India’s development journey. The ceremony was held in the august presence of the President of India, Smt. Droupadi Murmu, and attended by Principal Scientific Adviser to the Government of India Prof. Ajay Sood, CEO of NITI Aayog Nidhi Chhibber, senior officials of NITI Aayog and the Government of India, scientists, incubator partners and innovators from across the country. On the occasion, 26 grassroots innovators were honoured for developing practical, affordable and community-driven solutions across agriculture, healthcare, clean energy, assistive technology, water management, circular economy and sustainable livelihoods. Describing grassroots innovation as the true strength of India’s innovation ecosystem, Dr. Jitendra Singh said the country has today crossed 2.4 lakh startups, making it the world’s third-largest startup ecosystem. He said these achievements are significant, but the real success of India’s innovation movement will be measured by the number of real-life problems solved through affordable technologies that improve the lives of farmers, women, artisans, entrepreneurs and ordinary citizens. Innovations that reduce drudgery, enhance productivity, generate livelihoods and create sustainable local enterprises, he said, represent the true spirit of inclusive development. The Minister said Atal Community Innovation Centres (ACICs) have become an important bridge between community knowledge and the formal innovation ecosystem by providing mentoring, incubation, technical guidance, market linkages and capacity-building support to innovators from underserved regions. He noted that 25 ACICs are already operational while another 25 are under development, with the existing centres having supported more than 2,500 grassroots innovators. These centres are helping ensure that a promising idea is not constrained by geography, institutional access or lack of resources, but receives the support required to evolve into a viable enterprise. Dr. Jitendra Singh said the 26 innovators recognised this year represent the diversity and vibrancy of India’s grassroots innovation movement, coming from 16 States and 23 districts, ranging in age from 24 to 66 years, and including 11 women innovators. Their work addresses some of the country’s most pressing challenges through practical solutions in agriculture, healthcare, water conservation, clean energy, sustainable manufacturing, disability support and rural livelihoods, reaffirming that transformative innovation often emerges from close engagement with local communities and their everyday challenges. The innovations honoured during the ceremony reflect the breadth of India’s grassroots ingenuity. These include compact mini rice mills that enable small farmers to process produce at source, tractor-operated machines that reclaim uncultivable land, technologies converting agricultural residue into high-value bio-products, AI-enabled soil diagnostic services that improve farm productivity, biodegradable alternatives to single-use plastics manufactured from agricultural waste, affordable assistive technologies for persons with disabilities and decentralised clean energy solutions that strengthen rural livelihoods while promoting environmental sustainability. Emphasising the need to accelerate the journey from innovation to enterprise, Dr. Jitendra Singh called for stronger integration between the grassroots innovation ecosystem nurtured by AIM and the Department of Science and Technology’s National Initiative for Developing and Harnessing Innovations (NIDHI). Such convergence, he said, would provide innovators access to Technology Business Incubators, Centres of Excellence, prototype development, scientific validation, intellectual property support, product testing, certification, manufacturing partnerships, finance and market linkages, creating a robust national pathway from idea to product and from product to market. Referring to the experience of the National Innovation Foundation, the Minister said India has repeatedly demonstrated that grassroots ideas can achieve national recognition when backed by sustained institutional support. He cited the Mitticool refrigerator, which evolved from a traditional clay-based innovation into the basis of a Bureau of Indian Standards specification, as an example of how scientific validation, incubation and technology development can transform community knowledge into nationally accepted products. Calling upon scientists, academic institutions, incubators, industry and government departments to work in close partnership, Dr. Jitendra Singh said every recognised innovator should receive continued support through translation-readiness assessment, specialised incubation, design refinement, intellectual property facilitation, testing, certification and real-world pilot deployments. He said recognition should mark the beginning ‘not the destination’ of an innovator’s journey, enabling local ideas to scale into solutions of national relevance. Concluding, Dr. Jitendra Singh said India’s innovation ecosystem must become increasingly responsive to grassroots talent by reaching innovators where they are and strengthening their ability to solve local challenges through science and technology. He expressed confidence that with sustained institutional support and stronger collaboration across government, academia and industry, grassroots innovators will emerge as key partners in shaping an Atmanirbhar Bharat and a Viksit Bharat, ensuring that the country’s next generation of transformative ideas originates from every village, every district and every community across the nation. ***** NKR/AK (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2292453) आगंतुक पटल  : 128 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी , Tamil , Telugu Ministry of Science & Technology Dr. Jitendra Singh calls for connecting "Grassroots Innovators" with country's formal innovation ecosystem India’s Next Wave of Growth Will Emerge from Villages, Small Towns and Community Innovators: Dr. Jitendra Singh Grassroots Innovator Recognition Ceremony Honours 26 Innovators; Dr. Jitendra Singh Calls for National Innovation Pathway Local Solutions Must Evolve into National Enterprises to Realise Viksit Bharat: Dr. Jitendra Singh प्रविष्टि तिथि:

Calling for a seamless pathway to transform grassroots innovations into nationally scalable enterprises, he said innovation must move beyond recognition to scientific validation, technology translation, incubation and market adoption so that local solutions evolve into national assets capable of addressing India’s developmental priorities. Addressing the Grassroots Innovator Recognition Ceremony 2026 at the Rashtrapati Bhavan Cultural Centre, New Delhi, Dr. Jitendra Singh said the Government, under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, has transformed innovation into a nationwide movement by democratising access to science, technology and entrepreneurship. He said the Atal Innovation Mission (AIM) has expanded the innovation ecosystem beyond premier institutions and metropolitan centres, enabling talented innovators from rural, tribal, hilly, coastal, aspirational and remote regions to become active partners in India’s development journey. The ceremony was held in the august presence of the President of India, Smt. Droupadi Murmu, and attended by Principal Scientific Adviser to the Government of India Prof. Ajay Sood, CEO of NITI Aayog Nidhi Chhibber, senior officials of NITI Aayog and the Government of India, scientists, incubator partners and innovators from across the country. On the occasion, 26 grassroots innovators were honoured for developing practical, affordable and community-driven solutions across agriculture, healthcare, clean energy, assistive technology, water management, circular economy and sustainable livelihoods. Describing grassroots innovation as the true strength of India’s innovation ecosystem, Dr. Jitendra Singh said the country has today crossed 2.4 lakh startups, making it the world’s third-largest startup ecosystem. He said these achievements are significant, but the real success of India’s innovation movement will be measured by the number of real-life problems solved through affordable technologies that improve the lives of farmers, women, artisans, entrepreneurs and ordinary citizens. Innovations that reduce drudgery, enhance productivity, generate livelihoods and create sustainable local enterprises, he said, represent the true spirit of inclusive development. The Minister said Atal Community Innovation Centres (ACICs) have become an important bridge between community knowledge and the formal innovation ecosystem by providing mentoring, incubation, technical guidance, market linkages and capacity-building support to innovators from underserved regions. He noted that 25 ACICs are already operational while another 25 are under development, with the existing centres having supported more than 2,500 grassroots innovators. These centres are helping ensure that a promising idea is not constrained by geography, institutional access or lack of resources, but receives the support required to evolve into a viable enterprise. Dr. Jitendra Singh said the 26 innovators recognised this year represent the diversity and vibrancy of India’s grassroots innovation movement, coming from 16 States and 23 districts, ranging in age from 24 to 66 years, and including 11 women innovators. Their work addresses some of the country’s most pressing challenges through practical solutions in agriculture, healthcare, water conservation, clean energy, sustainable manufacturing, disability support and rural livelihoods, reaffirming that transformative innovation often emerges from close engagement with local communities and their everyday challenges. The innovations honoured during the ceremony reflect the breadth of India’s grassroots ingenuity. These include compact mini rice mills that enable small farmers to process produce at source, tractor-operated machines that reclaim uncultivable land, technologies converting agricultural residue into high-value bio-products, AI-enabled soil diagnostic services that improve farm productivity, biodegradable alternatives to single-use plastics manufactured from agricultural waste, affordable assistive technologies for persons with disabilities and decentralised clean energy solutions that strengthen rural livelihoods while promoting environmental sustainability. Emphasising the need to accelerate the journey from innovation to enterprise, Dr. Jitendra Singh called for stronger integration between the grassroots innovation ecosystem nurtured by AIM and the Department of Science and Technology’s National Initiative for Developing and Harnessing Innovations (NIDHI). Such convergence, he said, would provide innovators access to Technology Business Incubators, Centres of Excellence, prototype development, scientific validation, intellectual property support, product testing, certification, manufacturing partnerships, finance and market linkages, creating a robust national pathway from idea to product and from product to market. Referring to the experience of the National Innovation Foundation, the Minister said India has repeatedly demonstrated that grassroots ideas can achieve national recognition when backed by sustained institutional support. He cited the Mitticool refrigerator, which evolved from a traditional clay-based innovation into the basis of a Bureau of Indian Standards specification, as an example of how scientific validation, incubation and technology development can transform community knowledge into nationally accepted products. Calling upon scientists, academic institutions, incubators, industry and government departments to work in close partnership, Dr. Jitendra Singh said every recognised innovator should receive continued support through translation-readiness assessment, specialised incubation, design refinement, intellectual property facilitation, testing, certification and real-world pilot deployments. He said recognition should mark the beginning ‘not the destination’ of an innovator’s journey, enabling local ideas to scale into solutions of national relevance. Concluding, Dr. Jitendra Singh said India’s innovation ecosystem must become increasingly responsive to grassroots talent by reaching innovators where they are and strengthening their ability to solve local challenges through science and technology. He expressed confidence that with sustained institutional support and stronger collaboration across government, academia and industry, grassroots innovators will emerge as key partners in shaping an Atmanirbhar Bharat and a Viksit Bharat, ensuring that the country’s next generation of transformative ideas originates from every village, every district and every community across the nation. ***** NKR/AK (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2292453)

title: TDB-DST Supports M/s RoadGrid India Private Limited, Indore, for Commercialization of Indigenous Universal EV Charging Technology
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Science & Technology TDB-DST Supports M/s RoadGrid India Private Limited, Indore, for Commercialization of Indigenous Universal EV Charging Technology प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                31 JUL 2026 12:58PM by PIB Delhi As India accelerates its transition towards electric mobility, the Technology Development Board (TDB), under the Department of Science & Technology (DST), Government of India, has extended financial assistance to M/s RoadGrid India Private Limited, Indore, for the project titled “Setting up the Manufacturing and Assembly Facility for Commercialization of Universal EV Charger.” The project aims to establish indigenous manufacturing capabilities for next-generation universal EV chargers, strengthening India's charging infrastructure ecosystem while advancing the national vision of Aatmanirbhar Bharat and sustainable transportation. The project will establish a state-of-the-art manufacturing and assembly facility for commercial production of Universal EV Chargers capable of serving electric two-wheelers, three-wheelers, passenger vehicles, and commercial electric vehicles through a single integrated charging platform. The initiative seeks to address one of the key challenges in EV adoption by developing interoperable, high-performance charging infrastructure that supports multiple vehicle categories while reducing dependence on imported charging technologies. RoadGrid has developed a patented Universal EV Charger integrating 140 kW dual DC gun (CCS2 + Type 6) charging along with AC charging capability, enabling seamless charging for a wide range of electric vehicles. The project encompasses complete manufacturing and assembly of power electronics, thermal management systems, embedded software, communication modules, metering systems, control hardware, enclosure fabrication, quality testing, calibration, and final system integration. The manufacturing facility has also been designed with scalability to support future expansion into ultra-fast charging systems and integrated energy storage solutions. Founded in 2020, RoadGrid has emerged as an integrated EV charging technology company offering indigenous hardware, intelligent software platforms, and charging infrastructure services. The company is actively engaged in manufacturing EV chargers, deploying public charging infrastructure, and developing smart energy management solutions. Its recent strategic collaborations with leading industry stakeholders further reinforce its growing role in strengthening India's EV charging ecosystem. The project is expected to significantly enhance domestic manufacturing capacity for advanced EV charging equipment, promote import substitution in critical power electronics, and support the rapid expansion of public charging infrastructure across urban centres, highways, residential communities, and commercial fleet operations. By combining indigenous hardware with intelligent software and smart-grid integration, the initiative will contribute towards building a robust, interoperable, and future-ready EV charging network for the country. Speaking on the occasion, Shri Rajesh Kumar Pathak, Secretary, TDB, stated, "The rapid expansion of reliable and interoperable charging infrastructure is fundamental to accelerating electric mobility in India. Indigenous development and manufacturing of advanced EV charging technologies will strengthen the domestic clean mobility ecosystem, reduce import dependence, and support the country's transition towards sustainable transportation. TDB remains committed to supporting technology-driven enterprises that are building globally competitive solutions for India's green mobility future." Expressing gratitude for the support, the leadership of M/s RoadGrid India Private Limited stated that the assistance from TDB will enable the company to scale up manufacturing of its patented Universal EV Chargers, strengthen indigenous innovation in charging infrastructure, and accelerate the deployment of smart, reliable, and accessible EV charging solutions across the country. ****** NKR/FT (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2292264) आगंतुक पटल  : 172 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: हिन्दी , Tamil , Telugu Ministry of Science & Technology TDB-DST Supports M/s RoadGrid India Private Limited, Indore, for Commercialization of Indigenous Universal EV Charging Technology प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: TDB-DST Supports M/s Foodtechnics Pvt. Ltd., Bengaluru, for Commercialization of Indigenous Compact Automatic Roti Making Machine
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Science & Technology TDB-DST Supports M/s Foodtechnics Pvt. Ltd., Bengaluru, for Commercialization of Indigenous Compact Automatic Roti Making Machine प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                31 JUL 2026 12:56PM by PIB Delhi Advancing indigenous kitchen automation and smart food processing technologies, the Technology Development Board (TDB), under the Department of Science & Technology (DST), Government of India, has extended financial assistance to M/s Foodtechnics Pvt. Ltd., Bengaluru, for the project titled “ROTIDO – Compact Automatic Roti Making Machine with Inbuilt Kneader, Pressing and Roasting.” The project aims to commercialize a fully indigenous, compact automated roti-making system designed for households, small businesses, restaurants, and institutional kitchens, supporting India's vision of Aatmanirbhar Bharat through homegrown manufacturing and innovation. The project focuses on the development and commercialization of ROTIDO C-150, a compact, intelligent roti-making machine that integrates kneading, dough handling, pressing, roasting, and automatic ejection into a single automated system. Designed to produce up to 150 rotis per hour, the machine delivers consistent quality while significantly reducing manual effort, improving hygiene, and enhancing operational efficiency. The technology has been developed entirely through the company's in-house research and development efforts. Building on the successful commercialization of its larger industrial models, ROTIDO R-1000 and RS-1000, Foodtechnics is now introducing a compact solution specifically tailored for domestic users and small commercial establishments. The project has also received support under the NIDHI PRAYAS Scheme for prototype development, demonstrating a successful innovation journey from early-stage technology development to commercialization. A key innovation of the ROTIDO C-150 lies in its seamless integration of a 2 kg inbuilt kneader, automated dough ball feeding system, precision pressing mechanism, and three-layer controlled roasting technology within a compact footprint. Intelligent process synchronization, programmable controls, and an integrated dough weighing system ensure uniform thickness, consistent roasting, and repeatable product quality with minimal human intervention. The modular and energy-efficient design enables hygienic operation while making automated roti preparation accessible and affordable for a wider segment of users. The project is expected to strengthen India's domestic manufacturing ecosystem for food processing equipment by offering an indigenous alternative to imported automated kitchen solutions. Beyond improving convenience and productivity, the technology has the potential to support restaurants, cloud kitchens, hostels, hospitals, canteens, and small food enterprises by reducing labour dependency, improving food consistency, and enhancing operational efficiency. Speaking on the occasion, Shri Rajesh Kumar Pathak, Secretary, TDB, stated, "Innovation in food processing equipment is essential for improving productivity, hygiene, and ease of living while creating globally competitive manufacturing capabilities in India. Indigenous technologies such as ROTIDO demonstrate how engineering innovation can address everyday challenges through affordable automation. TDB is committed to supporting enterprises that are developing market-ready technologies with strong commercial potential and societal impact." Expressing gratitude for the support, the leadership of M/s Foodtechnics Pvt. Ltd. stated that TDB's assistance will accelerate the commercialization of the ROTIDO C-150 platform, strengthen domestic manufacturing capabilities, and enable wider adoption of indigenous automated food processing technologies across Indian households and small businesses. ***** NKR/FT (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2292262) आगंतुक पटल  : 122 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी , Telugu , Kannada Ministry of Science & Technology TDB-DST Supports M/s Foodtechnics Pvt. ministry: Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
title: Cabinet Approved Revised Policy for Award of Waterfront and Associated Land to Port Dependent Industries (PDI) in Major Ports
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways Cabinet Approved Revised Policy for Award of Waterfront and Associated Land to Port Dependent Industries (PDI) in Major Ports Revised Policy allows existing captive users to add new berth/jetty/terminal/single buoy mooring (SBM) for Enhanced Captive Requirement upto 30 years for Government entities Competitive bidding with RoFR to unlock fresh capacity expansion at major ports Government entities gain Direct Access to Waterfront under new policy प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                31 JUL 2026 7:38PM by PIB Delhi NEW DELHI, July 31, 2026: The Union Cabinet has approved a revised Policy for Award of Waterfront and Associated Land to Port Dependent Industries (Captive Policy), introducing a series of reforms aimed at accelerating private investment through the Public Private Partnership (PPP) model, improving operational flexibility and strengthening infrastructure development across India's major ports. The revised policy updates the existing Captive Policy of 2016 by enabling existing captive users to expand capacity through new berths, jetties, terminals and single buoy moorings (SBMs), while also providing a framework for extending concession agreements, awarding waterfront to eligible government entities and addressing changes arising from evolving business and regulatory conditions. Union Minister for Ports, Shipping and Waterways (MoPSW) Sarbananda Sonowal said the revised policy reflects the government's commitment to creating a predictable, transparent and investor-friendly framework for port-led industrial growth. "The revised Captive Policy is a major reform that balances investor confidence with public interest. By providing long-term certainty to existing operators, facilitating capacity expansion and creating a transparent framework for future investments, we are strengthening India's maritime infrastructure to support the country's rise as a global trade and logistics hub under the visionary leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi," Sonowal said. The policy is expected to provide greater certainty to investors, facilitate capacity augmentation and improve ease of doing business in the port sector without any financial implication for the Government. One of the key reforms allows Major Port Authorities to renew or extend concession agreements of existing Port Dependent Industries (PDIs) for up to 30 years without requiring a fresh tender process. The renewal will be undertaken at either the prevailing market rate or the indexed revenue payable under the existing concession agreement, whichever is higher, protecting port revenues while providing long-term certainty to investors. The policy also creates a structured mechanism for capacity expansion by existing captive users. Major Port Authorities will undertake price discovery through competitive bidding, while providing the existing concessionaire a Right of First Refusal (RoFR) to match the highest bid. Participation will be restricted to eligible Port Dependent Industries handling the same cargo profile, ensuring competitive price discovery while maintaining operational continuity. To prevent misuse of the expansion route for extending concession tenure, the concession period for any additional berth or terminal developed under the expansion proposal will remain co-terminus with the maximum permissible concession period of the existing facility. Waterfront Access for Government Bodies For the first time, the policy provides a framework for awarding waterfront and associated land to eligible government organisations without resorting to competitive bidding, subject to availability and prescribed safeguards. Eligible entities include Central and State Government departments, statutory authorities, autonomous bodies, Central and State Public Sector Undertakings (CPSUs and SPSUs), and government-controlled joint ventures operating in sectors such as fertilizers, food, petroleum, oil and gas, coal, steel and other sectors notified by the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways.The concessions will be awarded at the notified floor price. Recognising the evolving nature of global trade, the revised policy introduces provisions for Change in Law and Unforeseen Events, allowing business plans and cargo profiles to be revised where regulatory changes or unforeseen circumstances affect project viability. "The maritime sector operates in a dynamic global environment. This policy provides the flexibility needed to adapt to changing realities while ensuring continuity of investment, trade and port operations," said Union Minister Sarbananda Sonowal . The revised policy addresses key gaps in the 2016 framework by providing long-term certainty for investors, enabling capacity expansion in line with industrial demand and introducing greater operational flexibility for captive facilities. It also permits changes in cargo profile after the prescribed lock-in period, or immediately where necessitated by a change in law, ensuring business continuity in a dynamic global trading environment. The Government expects the reforms to catalyse fresh investment in port infrastructure, strengthen supply chains, reduce logistics risks for port-dependent industries and generate employment through expansion of port-led industrial activity. The policy will be implemented across all Major Ports and is expected to increase cargo throughput, improve utilisation of waterfront assets and generate sustained revenue for ports without any financial implication for the Government of India. The policy will be implemented across all Major Ports for captive facilities and is expected to improve cargo throughput, optimise utilisation of waterfront assets and generate sustained revenue for ports without any financial implication for the Government of India. *** MI/Indu (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2292692) आगंतुक पटल  : 70 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways Cabinet Approved Revised Policy for Award of Waterfront and Associated Land to Port Dependent Industries (PDI) in Major Ports Revised Policy allows existing captive users to add new berth/jetty/terminal/single buoy mooring (SBM) for Enhanced Captive Requirement upto 30 years for Government entities Competitive bidding with RoFR to unlock fresh capacity expansion at major ports Government entities gain Direct Access to Waterfront under new policy प्रविष्टि तिथि:

ministry: Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
title: GEOPOLITICAL DISRUPTIONS AND INLAND ECONOMIC CORRIDORS
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways GEOPOLITICAL DISRUPTIONS AND INLAND ECONOMIC CORRIDORS प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                31 JUL 2026 3:41PM by PIB Delhi The Government continuously monitors the impact of geopolitical developments on global maritime trade and logistics through institutional mechanisms involving the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways (MoPSW) and other concerned Ministries & Departments. An Inter-Ministerial Group (IMG), constituted under the Department of Commerce comprising of Ministry of External Aﬀairs (MEA), Ministry  of Ports, Shipping  and  Waterways (MoPS&W), Ministry  of  Civil  Aviation,  (MoCA), Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas (MoPNG), Reserve Bank of India (RBI), Central Board  of Indirect Taxes and  Customs (CBIC),  Export  Credit  Guarantee Corporation  of  India  (ECGC),  Department  for Promotion of Industry and  Internal Trade  (DPIIT), Agricultural & Processed Food Products   Export   Development   Authority   (APEDA),   Department   of   Financial Services (DFS),  and  Container Corporation  Of India  (CONCOR), regularly reviews the evolving situation, assesses its implications for maritime trade and supply chains, and facilitates coordinated action to address emerging challenges. The review mechanism covers issues relating to international shipping routes, movement of export-import cargo, port operations, logistics, freight and insurance costs, and the continuity of supply chains across sectors dependent on maritime trade. Based on these assessments, the Government has taken a number of coordinated measures to facilitate uninterrupted cargo movement and enhance supply-chain resilience, including operational support at major ports, waiver of ground rent and demurrage charges, facilitation of container evacuation through rail connectivity, trade facilitation measures, and initiatives to reduce logistics costs in coordination with the concerned Ministries, agencies and other stakeholders. Details of the measures taken are attached as Annexure . Annexure The measures taken by Government of India to facilitate uninterrupted cargo movement: Directorate General of Foreign Trade  (DGFT), under  the Department of Commerce, extended the  export  obligation period for the  Export  Promotion Capital  Goods  (EPCG)   and   Advance   Authorisation  Schemes  which  were expiring between March 01, 2026  and  May 31, 2026,  up to  August 31, 2026 covering 1,017  EPCG  and  7,400  Advance  Authorisations; restored RoDTEP rates;   discharged   export    obligation   of   21,370    EPCG    and    Advance authorisations  through   a   special  drive,  thereby  unlocking  funds  held  in pending  Bank  Guarantees. Agricultural & Processed Food Products Export Development Authority (APEDA) ran a helpline for exporters; Government allowed gems-and-jewellery import and vaulting in SEZs/FTWZs . Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC) issued clariﬁcations for returned and diverted cargo and extended fee waivers and cargo handling ﬂexibility up to June 30, 2026; Reserve Bank of India (RBI)/ Department of Financial Services (DFS) continued the extended export credit period from 270 to 450 days till June 05, 2026 and introduced Emergency Credit Line Guarantee Scheme (ECLGS) 5.0 for MSME liquidity. title: INDIGENOUS CONTAINER MANUFACTURING
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways INDIGENOUS CONTAINER MANUFACTURING प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                31 JUL 2026 3:39PM by PIB Delhi An order for shipping containers was placed by a global shipping line on an Indian container manufacturer. The domestically produced prototype container was unveiled at Dadri, Uttar Pradesh on 03.07.2026. The shipping containers are produced in accordance with internationally accepted quality and safety standards, including International Organization for Standardization (ISO) specifications and the International Convention for Safe Containers (CSC). The Government in Budget Speech 2026-27 has announced a Scheme for container manufacturing in India with a budget outlay of ₹ 10,000 crore aimed at creating globally competitive container manufacturing ecosystem in the country. The Union Budget of 2026 announced plans to operationalize 19 new National Waterways over the next five years, building upon the 32 national waterways that are already operational for cargo/ passenger movement out of a total network of 111 declared waterways. The Government has approved a comprehensive ₹69,725 crore package to strengthen domestic shipbuilding capacity, maritime financing, shipyard development, skilling, and reforms. Key components of the package include: Shipbuilding Financial Assistance Scheme (SBFAS), an extension of Shipbuilding Financial Assistance Policy (SBFAP), with outlay of ₹ 24,736 crore to address cost disadvantages of Indian shipyards vis-a-vis global shipyards . Maritime Development Fund (MDF) corpus of ₹ 25,000 crore for providing long term financing support to shipbuilding and maritime sector comprising a Maritime Investment Fund (MIF) of ₹ 20,000 crore and Interest Incentivisation Fund (IIF) of ₹ 5,000 crore . Shipbuilding Development Scheme (SbDS) with ₹19,989 crore outlay to expand Indian shipbuilding output capacity by setting up greenfield shipbuilding clusters and capacity expansion of the existing shipyards. Further, given the high employment multiplier of 6.4 in shipbuilding industry, the employment generation potential through these schemes is of around 2.2 million jobs including direct as well as indirect employment. This information was given by the Union Minister of Ports, Shipping and Waterways, Sarbananda Sonowal, in a written reply to the Lok Sabha. *** MI/Indu (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2292402) आगंतुक पटल  : 122 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी , Assamese , Assamese , Telugu Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways INDIGENOUS CONTAINER MANUFACTURING प्रविष्टि तिथि:
